title.zh: 卷一百十八 列傳第六十八: 元載 王昂 李少良 王縉 楊炎 黎幹 庾準
title.en: Volume 118 Biographies 68: Yuan Zai, Wan Gang, Li Shaoliang, Wang Jin, Yang Yan, Li Gan, Yu Zhun
title.raw: 卷一百十八 列傳第六十八: 元載 王昂 李少良 王縉 楊炎 黎幹 庾準 Volume 118 Biographies 68: Yuan Zai, Wan Gang, Li Shaoliang, Wang Jin, Yang Yan, Li Gan, Yu Zhun

sentences.zh: 元載王昂李少良郇謨附

translations.literal: Yuan Zai, Wang Ang, Li Shaoliang, Huan Mo, appended.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Zai, Wang Ang, Li Shaoliang, and Huan Mo, appended biography.

sentences.zh: 王縉楊炎黎幹劉忠翼附

translations.literal: Wang Jin, Yang Yan, Li Gan, Liu Zhongyi, appended.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jin, Yang Yan, Li Gan, and Liu Zhongyi, appended biography.

sentences.zh: 元載，鳳翔岐山人也，家本寒微。

translations.literal: Yuan Zai was a native of Qishan in Fengxiang; his family was originally poor and humble.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Zai was a native of Qishan in Fengxiang Prefecture, from a family of modest means.

sentences.zh: 父景昇，任員外官，不理產業，常居岐州。

translations.literal: His father Jing Sheng held an extra-official post, did not manage family property, and usually lived in Qi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jing Sheng held an honorary official title, neglected the family estate, and lived mostly in Qi Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 載母攜載適景昇，冒姓元氏。

translations.literal: Zai's mother brought Zai to marry Jing Sheng and took the surname Yuan falsely.
translations.idiomatic: Zai's mother brought him to Jing Sheng when she remarried, and the boy took the surname Yuan.

sentences.zh: 載自幼嗜學，好屬文，性敏惠，博覽子史，尤學道書。

translations.literal: From youth Zai loved learning, was fond of literary composition, was by nature quick and clever, broadly read histories and the masters, and especially studied Daoist texts.
translations.idiomatic: From childhood Zai was devoted to study, fond of writing, quick-witted by nature, widely read in histories and the classics, and especially versed in Daoist writings.

sentences.zh: 家貧，徒步隨鄉賦，累上不升第。

translations.literal: The family was poor; he went on foot to follow the local examination levy and repeatedly failed to pass.
translations.idiomatic: Poor as they were, he walked to the provincial examinations year after year and never passed.

sentences.zh: 天寶初，玄宗崇奉道教，下詔求明莊、老、文、列四子之學者。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Tianbao era, Xuanzong revered Daoism and issued an edict seeking scholars versed in Zhuangzi, Laozi, Wenzi, and Liezi.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tianbao reign, Emperor Xuanzong promoted Daoism and issued an edict calling for experts in Zhuangzi, Laozi, Wenzi, and Liezi.

sentences.zh: 載策入高科，授邠州新平尉。

translations.literal: Zai entered by examination with a high grade and was appointed Wei of Xinping in Bin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zai passed the special examination with high marks and was appointed magistrate of Xinping in Bin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 監察御史韋鎰充使監選黔中，引載為判官，載名稍著，遷大理評事。

translations.literal: Supervising Censor Wei Yi served as envoy overseeing selection in Qianzhong and brought Zai in as aide; Zai's name gradually became known, and he was promoted to Evaluator of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: When Supervising Censor Wei Yi went to Qianzhong as selection commissioner, he took Zai on as his aide. Zai's reputation grew, and he was promoted to judicial reviewer in the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 東都留守苗晉卿又引為判官，遷大理司直。

translations.literal: Eastern Capital Intendant Miao Jinqing again brought him in as aide, and he was promoted to Directing Censor of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Capital Intendant Miao Jinqing also took him on as aide, after which he rose to directing censor in the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 肅宗即位，急於軍務，諸道廉使隨才擢用。

translations.literal: When Suzong took the throne, urgent over military affairs, integrity commissioners of the various circuits were promoted according to ability.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Suzong came to the throne, military needs were urgent, and integrity commissioners across the circuits were promoted on merit.

sentences.zh: 時載避地江左，蘇州刺史、江東采訪使李希言表載為副，拜祠部員外郎，遷洪州刺史。

translations.literal: At the time Zai had fled to the lands south of the Yangzi; Suzhou Prefect and Jiangdong Investigation Commissioner Li Xiyan recommended Zai as deputy, and he was appointed Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites, then transferred to Prefect of Hong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zai had taken refuge in the lower Yangzi region. Li Xiyan, prefect of Suzhou and Jiangdong investigation commissioner, recommended him as deputy; Zai was appointed vice director in the Ministry of Rites and later became prefect of Hong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 兩京平，入為度支郎中。

translations.literal: When the two capitals were pacified, he entered the capital as Director of the Bureau of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: After the two capitals were recovered, he entered court service as director in the Bureau of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 載智性敏悟，善奏對，肅宗嘉之，委以國計，俾充使江、淮，都領漕輓之任，尋加御史中丞。

translations.literal: Zai was intelligent and quick to understand, skilled at memorial responses; Suzong praised him, entrusted him with state finance, made him envoy to the Jiang and Huai regions to oversee overall transport of grain tribute, and soon added Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Quick-witted and articulate in memorials, Zai won Suzong's favor. The emperor entrusted him with national finances, sent him as envoy to the Jiang and Huai regions to oversee grain transport, and soon made him vice censor-in-chief as well.

sentences.zh: 數月征入，遷戶部侍郎、度支使並諸道轉運使。

translations.literal: Within several months he was summoned to court and promoted to Vice Minister of Revenue, Commissioner of Revenue, and Transport Commissioner for all circuits.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few months he was recalled to court and promoted to vice minister of revenue, revenue commissioner, and transport commissioner for all circuits.

sentences.zh: 既至朝廷，會肅宗寢疾。

translations.literal: Once he reached court, it happened that Suzong fell gravely ill.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly after he arrived at court, Emperor Suzong fell seriously ill.

sentences.zh: 載與幸臣李輔國善。

translations.literal: Zai was on good terms with the favored minister Li Fuguo.
translations.idiomatic: Zai was on close terms with the emperor's favorite, Li Fuguo.

sentences.zh: 輔國妻元氏，載之諸宗，因是相昵狎。

translations.literal: Fuguo's wife was of the Yuan clan, a kinswoman of Zai's, and because of this they were intimate and familiar.
translations.idiomatic: Fuguo's wife was a Yuan, a kinswoman of Zai's clan, and through her the two men grew intimate.

sentences.zh: 時輔國權傾海內，舉無違者，會選京尹，輔國乃以載兼京兆尹。

translations.literal: At the time Fuguo's power tilted the realm; nothing he did was opposed. When the capital intendant was to be chosen, Fuguo had Zai serve concurrently as Metropolitan Prefect of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Fuguo's authority then dominated the empire, and none dared oppose him. When a new capital intendant was to be chosen, Fuguo had Zai appointed concurrently as metropolitan prefect of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 載意屬國柄，詣輔國懇辭京尹，輔國識其意，然之。

translations.literal: Zai's intent lay on the reins of state; he went to Fuguo and earnestly declined the capital prefecture. Fuguo understood his meaning and approved.
translations.idiomatic: Zai had his eye on supreme power. He went to Fuguo and begged to be released from the capital prefecture; Fuguo understood and agreed.

sentences.zh: 翌日拜載同中書門下平章事，度支轉運使如故。

translations.literal: The next day Zai was appointed Associate Director of the Secretariat-Chancellery, his posts as revenue and transport commissioner remaining as before.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Zai was appointed associate director of the Secretariat-Chancellery while retaining his revenue and transport posts.

sentences.zh: 旬日，肅宗晏駕，代宗即位，輔國勢愈重，稱載於上前。

translations.literal: Within ten days Suzong passed away; Daizong took the throne; Fuguo's power grew still heavier, and he praised Zai before the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Ten days later Suzong died and Daizong succeeded him. Fuguo's influence grew even greater, and he spoke highly of Zai before the new emperor.

sentences.zh: 載能伺上意，頗承恩遇，遷中書侍郎、同中書門下平章事，加集賢殿大學士，修國史。

translations.literal: Zai could discern the emperor's intent and received considerable favor; he was promoted to Vice Director of the Secretariat, Associate Director of the Secretariat-Chancellery, made Grand Academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, and charged with compiling the national history.
translations.idiomatic: Skilled at reading the emperor's mind, Zai enjoyed growing favor. He was promoted to vice director of the Secretariat and associate director of the Secretariat-Chancellery, made grand academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, and put in charge of the national history.

sentences.zh: 又加銀青光祿大夫，封許昌縣子。

translations.literal: He was further given Silver-Gleaming Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and enfeoffed as Viscount of Xuchang County.
translations.idiomatic: He was also granted the title Silver-Gleaming Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and enfeoffed as Viscount of Xuchang.

sentences.zh: 載以度支轉運使職務繁碎，負荷且重，慮傷名，阻大位，素與劉晏相友善，乃悉以錢谷之務委之，薦晏自代，載自加營田使。

translations.literal: Zai considered the duties of revenue and transport commissioner numerous and trivial, burdensome and heavy, and feared they would harm his reputation and block the great post. He had long been friendly with Liu Yan, so he entrusted all fiscal grain affairs to him, recommended Yan to replace himself, and Zai added for himself the post of Commissioner of Military Farms.
translations.idiomatic: Zai found the revenue and transport posts tedious and burdensome and feared they would tarnish his standing and block his rise. He had long been friendly with Liu Yan, so he handed all fiscal and grain duties to Yan, recommended Yan as his replacement, and took the military farms commission for himself.

sentences.zh: 李輔國罷職，又加判天下元帥行軍司馬。

translations.literal: When Li Fuguo was removed from office, Zai was further made Acting Chief of Staff to the Commander-in-Chief of All Forces.
translations.idiomatic: After Li Fuguo was dismissed, Zai was also made acting chief of staff to the commander-in-chief of all forces.

sentences.zh: 廣德元年，與宰臣劉晏、裴遵慶同扈從至陜。

translations.literal: In the first year of Guangde, together with chief ministers Liu Yan and Pei Zunqing he accompanied the emperor to Shan.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangde 1, 763, he accompanied the emperor to Shan Prefecture together with chief ministers Liu Yan and Pei Zunqing.

sentences.zh: 及輿駕還宮，遵慶皆罷所任，載恩寵彌盛。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage returned to the palace, Zunqing and the others were all removed from their posts, while Zai's favor grew ever greater.
translations.idiomatic: When the court returned to the capital, Zunqing and the others were dismissed, while Zai's favor only increased.

sentences.zh: 輔國死，載復結內侍董秀，多與之金帛，委主書卓英倩潛通密旨。

translations.literal: After Fuguo died, Zai again allied with the inner attendant Dong Xiu, gave him much gold and silk, and entrusted the chief secretary Zhuo Yingqian to convey secret orders.
translations.idiomatic: After Fuguo's death, Zai cultivated the inner attendant Dong Xiu with lavish gifts of gold and silk and used chief secretary Zhuo Yingqian to relay private instructions.

sentences.zh: 以是上有所屬，載必先知之，承意探微，言必玄合，上益信任之。

translations.literal: Thus whenever the emperor had a preference, Zai always knew it beforehand; he followed intent and probed subtleties, and his words always matched mysteriously, so the emperor trusted him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the emperor formed a preference, Zai seemed to know it in advance. He read every nuance of the emperor's mood, and his words always struck the right note, so the emperor trusted him ever more deeply.

sentences.zh: 妻王氏狠戾自專，載出朝謁，縱子伯和等遊於外，上封人顧繇奏之，上方任載以政，反罪繇而已。

translations.literal: His wife Lady Wang was fierce and willful on her own; when Zai went out to court audience, she let sons Bohe and others roam outside. A sealed memorialist Gu Yao reported this. The emperor was then entrusting Zai with government and instead punished Yao only.
translations.idiomatic: His wife Lady Wang was brutal and domineering. While Zai attended court, she let their sons Bohe and others run wild in the city. When memorialist Gu Yao reported this, the emperor, still relying on Zai for government, punished Yao instead.

sentences.zh: 內侍魚朝恩負恃權寵，不與載協，載常憚之。

translations.literal: The inner attendant Yu Chao'en relied on favor and power and did not cooperate with Zai; Zai often feared him.
translations.idiomatic: The inner attendant Yu Chao'en, secure in imperial favor, refused to work with Zai, who feared him.

sentences.zh: 大歷四年冬，乘間密奏朝恩專權不軌，請除之。

translations.literal: In the winter of the fourth year of Dali, seizing an opportunity he secretly memorialized that Chao'en monopolized power and acted improperly, and asked that he be removed.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of Dali 4, 769, he seized an opening to memorialize secretly that Chao'en abused his power and asked that he be eliminated.

sentences.zh: 朝恩驕橫，天下鹹怒，上亦知之，及聞載奏，適會於心。

translations.literal: Chao'en was arrogant and overbearing; all under Heaven were angry, and the emperor also knew it. When he heard Zai's memorial, it happened to accord with his mind.
translations.idiomatic: Chao'en's arrogance had enraged the empire, and the emperor knew it well. Zai's memorial matched exactly what he had been thinking.

sentences.zh: 載遂結北軍大將同謀，以防萬慮。

translations.literal: Zai then allied with a great general of the northern armies in conspiracy, to guard against every contingency.
translations.idiomatic: Zai then conspired with a senior general of the northern armies to cover every contingency.

sentences.zh: 五年三月，朝恩伏法，度支使第五琦以朝恩黨坐累，載兼判度支，志氣自若，謂己有除惡之功，是非前賢，以為文武才略，莫己之若。

translations.literal: In the third month of the fifth year, Chao'en was executed by law. Revenue Commissioner Diwu Qi was implicated as Chao'en's partisan; Zai concurrently judged revenue affairs. His spirit was as before; he thought he had the merit of removing evil, disparaged former worthies, and believed that in civil and military talent and strategy none compared to himself.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of Dali 5, 770, Chao'en was executed. Revenue commissioner Diwu Qi was implicated as his partisan, and Zai took over revenue affairs himself. Complacent in triumph, Zai credited himself with ridding the court of evil, belittled his predecessors, and considered himself without peer in civil and military ability.

sentences.zh: 外委胥吏，內聽婦言。

translations.literal: Outwardly he entrusted clerks; inwardly he listened to his wife's words.
translations.idiomatic: He left public affairs to clerks and took his wife's counsel at home.

sentences.zh: 城中開南北二甲第，室宇宏麗，冠絕當時。

translations.literal: Within the city he opened two great mansions, north and south; their halls and rooms were grand and splendid, surpassing all of the time.
translations.idiomatic: He built two grand mansions in the capital, north and south of the city, whose scale and splendor surpassed anything of the age.

sentences.zh: 又於近郊起亭榭，所至之處，帷帳什器，皆於宿設，儲不改供。

translations.literal: He also raised pavilions and towers in the near suburbs; wherever he went, curtains, utensils, and furnishings were all set up the night before, stores unchanged in supply.
translations.idiomatic: He also built pavilions in the suburbs, with furnishings and supplies laid out overnight wherever he intended to go, so that nothing ever ran short.

sentences.zh: 城南膏腴別墅，連疆接畛，凡數十所，婢仆曳羅綺一百余人，恣為不法，侈僭無度。

translations.literal: South of the city were rich suburban villas, boundaries joining boundaries, several tens in all; maids and servants trailing brocades numbered more than a hundred; they did as they pleased unlawfully, extravagant and presumptuous beyond measure.
translations.idiomatic: He owned dozens of fertile estates south of the city, staffed by more than a hundred servants in silk, who broke the law at will in unrestrained extravagance.

sentences.zh: 江、淮方面，京輦要司，皆排去忠良，引用貪猥。

translations.literal: In the Jiang and Huai regions and in key offices of the capital area, he removed the loyal and good and brought in the greedy and base.
translations.idiomatic: Across the Jiang-Huai region and in key capital offices, he drove out the upright and installed the corrupt.

sentences.zh: 士有求進者，不結子弟，則謁主書，貨賄公行，近年以來，未有其比。

translations.literal: Scholars seeking advancement, if they did not attach themselves to his sons, then visited his chief secretaries; bribes circulated openly—in recent years there had been nothing like it.
translations.idiomatic: Officials seeking promotion had to court his sons or his secretaries; bribery was open and rampant to a degree unmatched in recent memory.

sentences.zh: 與王縉同列，縉方務聚財，遂睦於載，二人相得甚歡，日益縱橫。

translations.literal: He shared rank with Wang Jin; Jin was then bent on amassing wealth, so he became close with Zai. The two got on very well and daily grew more unrestrained.
translations.idiomatic: He served alongside Wang Jin, who was then bent on amassing wealth. The two became close allies and together grew ever more brazen.

sentences.zh: 代宗盡察其跡，以載任寄多年，欲全君臣之分，載嘗獨見，上誡之，不悛。

translations.literal: Daizong fully perceived his tracks. Because Zai had been entrusted for many years, he wished to preserve the lord-and-minister bond. Zai was once received alone; the emperor admonished him, but he did not repent.
translations.idiomatic: Daizong saw through him completely, yet because Zai had served so long he wished to preserve the bond between ruler and minister. On one private audience the emperor warned him, but Zai would not reform.

sentences.zh: 初，扈駕自陜還，與縉上表，請以河中府為中都，秋杪行幸，春首還京，以避蕃戎侵軼之患。

translations.literal: Earlier, when escorting the emperor back from Shan, together with Jin he submitted a memorial asking that Hezhong Prefecture be made central capital: an autumn tour there and return to the capital in early spring, to avoid the trouble of Tibetan and Rong incursions.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, on the return from Shan, he and Jin memorialized to make Hezhong the secondary capital—court to move there in late autumn and return in early spring to escape Tibetan raids.

sentences.zh: 帝初納之，遣條奏以聞。

translations.literal: The emperor at first accepted it and ordered a detailed memorial submitted for his information.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor initially agreed and asked for a detailed plan.

sentences.zh: 自魚朝恩就誅，誌頗盈滿，遂抗表請建中都，文多不載。

translations.literal: Since Yu Chao'en was executed, his ambition was quite full; he then submitted a defiant memorial asking to establish a central capital—the text is mostly not recorded.
translations.idiomatic: After Chao'en's execution his ambition swelled, and he submitted a bold memorial to establish the secondary capital; most of the text is not preserved.

sentences.zh: 大略以關輔、河東等十州戶稅入奉京師，創置精兵五萬，管在中都，以威四方，辭多開合。

translations.literal: In outline: household taxes of ten prefectures including Guanfu and Hedong were to supply the capital; fifty thousand elite troops were to be newly established and stationed at the central capital to awe the four quarters—the rhetoric was much open and closed.
translations.idiomatic: In outline he proposed routing taxes from ten prefectures including the capital region and Hedong to fund the court, creating fifty thousand elite troops stationed at the secondary capital to overawe the realm—the rhetoric was elaborate and evasive.

sentences.zh: 自以為表入事行，潛遣所由吏於河中經營。

translations.literal: He himself thought that once the memorial entered, the matter would proceed, and secretly sent his responsible clerks to Hezhong to make arrangements.
translations.idiomatic: Confident the plan would be approved, he secretly sent agents to Hezhong to begin preparations.

sentences.zh: 節度寄理於涇州。

translations.literal: The military commission was provisionally administered from Jing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The frontier command was temporarily administered from Jing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 大歷八年，蕃戎入邠寧之後，朝議以為三輔已西，無襟帶之固，而涇州散地，不足為守。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Dali, after the Tibetans and Rong entered Binning, court discussion held that west of the three adjunct metropolitan areas there was no solid strategic belt, while Jing Prefecture was scattered territory insufficient for defense.
translations.idiomatic: In Dali 8, 773, after Tibetan forces entered Binning, the court concluded that the region west of the capital lacked a secure defensive belt and that scattered Jing Prefecture was inadequate to hold the line.

sentences.zh: 載嘗為西州刺史，知河西、隴右之要害，指畫於上前曰：「今國家西境極於潘源，吐蕃防戍在摧沙堡，而原州界其間。

translations.literal: Zai had once been Prefect of Xi Prefecture and knew the strategic points of Hexi and Longyou. He pointed and drew before the emperor, saying: 'Now the state's western border ends at Panyuan; Tibetan garrisons are at Cuisha Fort, and Yuan Prefecture lies between them.'
translations.idiomatic: Zai had once served as prefect of Xi Prefecture and knew the Hexi and Longyou frontier. He explained to the emperor: 'Our western border now ends at Panyuan. Tibetan garrisons hold Cuisha Fort, with Yuan Prefecture between them.'

sentences.zh: 原州當西塞之口，接隴山之固，草肥水甘，舊壘存焉。

translations.literal: Yuan Prefecture stands at the mouth of the western frontier pass, joins the solidity of Long Mountain, has rich grass and sweet water, and old ramparts remain there.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Prefecture guards the western frontier pass, adjoins the strong position of Long Mountain, enjoys rich pasture and good water, and still has old fortifications.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃比毀其垣墉，棄之不居。

translations.literal: The Tibetans had recently destroyed its walls and ditches and abandoned it without occupying it.
translations.idiomatic: The Tibetans had recently destroyed its walls and abandoned the site.

sentences.zh: 其西則監牧故地，皆有長濠巨塹，重復深固。

translations.literal: West of it are the old pasture-commission lands, all with long moats and great trenches, layered and deeply solid.
translations.idiomatic: To the west lie the old imperial pasture lands, all with deep moats and trenches in multiple lines of defense.

sentences.zh: 原州雖早霜，黍稷不藝，而有平涼附其東，獨耕一縣，可以足食。

translations.literal: Although Yuan Prefecture has early frost and millet and grain are not cultivated, Pingliang adjoins it on the east; farming one county alone can suffice for food.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Prefecture suffers early frost and cannot grow grain, but Pingliang to the east could supply enough food from a single county's harvest.

sentences.zh: 請移京西軍戍原州，乘間築之，貯粟一年。

translations.literal: He asked to move the Capital-West Army to garrison Yuan Prefecture, seize an interval to build it, and store grain for one year.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed moving the Capital-West Army to garrison Yuan, rebuilding the fort when opportunity allowed, and stockpiling a year's grain.

sentences.zh: 戎人夏牧多在青海，羽書覆至，已逾月矣。

translations.literal: The Rong people's summer pastures are mostly at Qinghai; urgent dispatches have piled up for more than a month already.
translations.idiomatic: The Tibetans pasture in Qinghai in summer; urgent reports have been arriving for more than a month.

sentences.zh: 今運築並作，不二旬可畢。

translations.literal: Now transport and construction can be done together; in less than twenty days it can be finished.
translations.idiomatic: Transport and construction together could be finished in under twenty days.

sentences.zh: 移子儀大軍居涇，以為根本。

translations.literal: Move Guo Ziyi's great army to dwell at Jing as the root foundation.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi's main force should be stationed at Jing as the strategic base.

sentences.zh: 分兵守石門、木峽、隴山之關，北抵於河，皆連山峻嶺，寇不可越。

translations.literal: Divide troops to guard the passes of Shimen, Muxia, and Long Mountain; north to the river—all are linked mountains and steep ridges, and invaders cannot cross.
translations.idiomatic: Detach troops to hold the passes at Shimen, Muxia, and Long Mountain, north to the Yellow River—all rugged terrain the enemy could not cross.

sentences.zh: 稍置鳴沙縣、豐安軍為之羽翼，北帶靈武五城為之形勢。

translations.literal: Gradually establish Mingsha County and Feng'an Army as its wings; north, take the five cities of Lingwu as its strategic posture.
translations.idiomatic: Establish Mingsha County and Feng'an Army as supporting positions, with the five cities of Lingwu to the north completing the defensive layout.

sentences.zh: 然後舉隴右之地以至安西，是謂斷西戎之脛，朝廷可高枕矣。

translations.literal: Then raise the lands of Longyou as far as Anxi—this is called severing the shank of the western Rong, and the court can rest on high pillows.
translations.idiomatic: Then advance through Longyou to Anxi—cutting the Tibetan foothold so the court could rest secure.

sentences.zh: 」兼圖其地形以獻。

translations.literal: He also drew its terrain and presented it.
translations.idiomatic: He also submitted a map of the terrain.

sentences.zh: 載密使人逾隴山，入原州，量井泉，計徒庸，車乘畚鍤之器皆具。

translations.literal: Zai secretly sent men over Long Mountain into Yuan Prefecture to measure wells and springs, calculate labor and corvée, and prepare carts, shovels, and tools.
translations.idiomatic: Zai secretly sent agents over Long Mountain into Yuan to survey wells and springs, calculate labor needs, and prepare carts, tools, and equipment.

sentences.zh: 檢校左僕射田神功沮之曰：「夫興師料敵，老將所難。

translations.literal: Acting Left Vice Director Tian Shenggong obstructed him, saying: 'Raising armies and estimating the enemy is what old generals find difficult.'
translations.idiomatic: Acting Left Vice Director Tian Shenggong objected: 'Estimating the enemy before committing troops is what seasoned generals find hardest.'

sentences.zh: 陛下信一書生言，舉國從之，聽誤矣。

translations.literal: 'Your Majesty trusts one scholar's words and has the whole state follow—if you heed this, you err.'
translations.idiomatic: 'Your Majesty would trust a scholar's word and commit the whole empire to it—that would be a grave mistake.'

sentences.zh: 」上遲疑不決，會載得罪乃止。

translations.literal: The emperor hesitated and could not decide; it happened that Zai fell into guilt and then it stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor hesitated, and when Zai later fell from power the plan was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 初，六年，載條奏應緣別敕授文武六品以下，敕出後望令吏部、兵部便附甲團奏，不得檢勘，從之。

translations.literal: Earlier, in the sixth year, Zai submitted detailed items: for special-edict appointments of civil and military officials of the sixth rank and below, after the edict issued he hoped the Ministries of Personnel and War would promptly attach registers and submit in group memorial without examination—this was approved.
translations.idiomatic: In Dali 6, 771, Zai memorialized that for special-edict appointments of officials of the sixth rank and below, the Ministries of Personnel and War should register and submit them in batch without review. The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 時功狀奏擬，結銜多謬，載欲權歸於己，慮有司駁正。

translations.literal: At the time merit reports and draft submissions had many errors in joint signatures; Zai wished power to return to himself and feared the responsible offices would reject and correct them.
translations.idiomatic: Merit reports and nominations were often flawed, and Zai wanted sole control, fearing that the ministries would overturn his appointments.

sentences.zh: 會有上封人李少良密以載醜跡聞，載知之，奏於上前，少良等數人悉斃於公府。

translations.literal: It happened that a sealed memorialist Li Shaoliang secretly reported Zai's ugly tracks; Zai learned of it, memorialized before the emperor, and Shaoliang and several others were all beaten to death in the public offices.
translations.idiomatic: When sealed memorialist Li Shaoliang secretly reported Zai's misconduct, Zai learned of it, informed the emperor, and Shaoliang and several others were beaten to death in the government offices.

sentences.zh: 由是道路以目，不敢議載之短。

translations.literal: From this people on the roads exchanged glances and did not dare discuss Zai's faults.
translations.idiomatic: After that people exchanged fearful glances in the streets and dared not criticize Zai openly.

sentences.zh: 門庭之內，非其黨與不接，平素交友，涉於道義者悉疏棄之。

translations.literal: Within his gates, those not of his faction were not received; old friends who touched on righteousness were all cast off.
translations.idiomatic: At his gate he admitted only his own faction and cast off old friends who still spoke of principle.

sentences.zh: 代宗寬仁明恕，審其所由，凡累年，載長惡不悛，眾怒上聞。

translations.literal: Daizong was lenient, benevolent, clear, and forgiving, and examined what led to this. For several years Zai persisted in evil without repenting, and public anger reached the emperor's ears.
translations.idiomatic: Daizong was lenient and perceptive, and for years he watched Zai persist in wrongdoing while public outrage mounted.

sentences.zh: 大歷十二年三月庚辰，仗下後，上御延英殿，命左金吾大將軍吳湊收載、縉於政事堂，各留系本所，並中書主事卓英倩、李待榮及載男仲武、季能並收禁，命吏部尚書劉晏訊鞫。

translations.literal: On gengchen, the third month of the twelfth year of Dali, after the guard review, the emperor attended Yanying Hall, ordered Left Golden Guard General Wu Cou to seize Zai and Jin in the Hall of Administration, each detained at his own office; also Secretariat chief clerks Zhuo Yingqian and Li Dairong and Zai's sons Zhongwu and Jineng were all seized and imprisoned; ordered Minister of Personnel Liu Yan to interrogate.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen day in the third month of Dali 12, 777, after the morning review the emperor went to Yanying Hall and ordered Left Golden Guard General Wu Cou to arrest Zai and Jin in the Hall of Administration. Chief secretaries Zhuo Yingqian and Li Dairong and Zai's sons Zhongwu and Jineng were also seized. Minister of Personnel Liu Yan was ordered to conduct the inquiry.

sentences.zh: 晏以載受任樹黨，布於天下，不敢專斷，請他官共事。

translations.literal: Yan said that because Zai had received appointment and planted factions spread through the realm, he dared not decide alone and asked other officials to join the work.
translations.idiomatic: Yan said that because Zai's faction extended throughout the empire, he dared not judge alone and asked other officials to join the investigation.

sentences.zh: 敕御史大夫李涵、右散騎常侍蕭昕、兵部侍郎袁傪、禮部侍郎常袞、諫議大夫杜亞同推究其狀。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Censor-in-Chief Li Han, Right Regular Attendant Xiao Xin, Vice Minister of War Yuan Kai, Vice Minister of Rites Chang Gun, and Remonstrance Grand Master Du Ya jointly to pursue and examine the facts.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Censor-in-Chief Li Han, Right Regular Attendant Xiao Xin, Vice Minister of War Yuan Kai, Vice Minister of Rites Chang Gun, and Remonstrance Grand Master Du Ya to investigate together.

sentences.zh: 辯罪問端，皆出自禁中，仍遣中使詰以陰事，載、縉皆伏罪。

translations.literal: Debating guilt and questioning points all came from within the forbidden quarters; inner envoys were still sent to interrogate on secret matters, and Zai and Jin both confessed guilt.
translations.idiomatic: The charges and interrogation all came from within the palace. Inner envoys questioned them on secret matters, and both Zai and Jin confessed.

sentences.zh: 是日，宦官左衛將軍、知內侍省事董秀與載同惡，先載於禁中杖殺之。

translations.literal: That day the eunuch Left Guard General and Director of Palace Attendants Dong Xiu, who shared evil with Zai, was beaten to death in the forbidden quarters before Zai.
translations.idiomatic: That same day the eunuch Dong Xiu, Zai's accomplice, was beaten to death in the palace before Zai's own execution.

sentences.zh: 敕曰：「任直去邪，懸於帝典；

translations.literal: An edict said: 'Employing the upright and removing the crooked hangs in the imperial canon;
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared: 'To employ the upright and remove the wicked is set forth in the imperial canon;

sentences.zh: 獎善懲惡，急於時政。

translations.literal: rewarding good and punishing evil is urgent in timely government.'
translations.idiomatic: rewarding good and punishing evil is urgent to sound government.

sentences.zh: 和鼎之寄，匪易其人。

translations.literal: The charge of the harmonizing cauldron is not easily given to a man.
translations.idiomatic: The burden of harmonizing the state is not easily borne.

sentences.zh: 中書侍郎、同中書門下平章事元載，性頗奸回，跡非正直。

translations.literal: Vice Director of the Secretariat and Associate Director Yuan Zai's nature was quite treacherous and crooked; his tracks were not upright.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director of the Secretariat and Associate Director Yuan Zai was by nature treacherous and his conduct far from upright.

sentences.zh: 寵待逾分，早踐鈞衡。

translations.literal: Favor and treatment exceeded measure; he early trod the balance beam of state.
translations.idiomatic: Favored beyond measure, he rose early to the highest office.

sentences.zh: 亮弼之功，未能經邦成務；

translations.literal: His merit as a bright assistant could not bring the state through its tasks;
translations.idiomatic: His service as chief minister failed to govern the realm;

sentences.zh: 挾邪之誌，常以罔上面欺。

translations.literal: his heart holding crooked intent constantly deceived and faced upward to cheat.
translations.idiomatic: his crooked heart constantly deceived his sovereign.

sentences.zh: 陰托妖巫，夜行解禱，用圖非望，庶逭典章。

translations.literal: He secretly relied on sorcerers and shamans, went out at night for release-prayers, using them to seek what was not his to hope for, hoping to escape the statutes.
translations.idiomatic: He secretly employed sorcerers and went out at night for ritual prayers, seeking unlawful ends and hoping to escape the law.

sentences.zh: 納受贓私，貿鬻官秩。

translations.literal: He accepted bribes and private gain and traded and sold official ranks.
translations.idiomatic: He took bribes and sold offices.

sentences.zh: 兇妻忍害，暴子侵牟，曾不提防，恣其淩虐。

translations.literal: His fierce wife was cruel and harmful; his violent sons encroached and extorted; he never guarded against them and let them rampage and abuse at will.
translations.idiomatic: His brutal wife and violent sons preyed on the people, and he never restrained their abuses.

sentences.zh: 行僻辭矯，心狠貌恭，使沈抑之流，無因自達，賞罰差謬，罔不由茲。

translations.literal: His conduct was devious and his words pretentious; his heart was harsh though his face respectful, so that those sunk and suppressed had no means to advance themselves; rewards and punishments were wrongly applied—all arose from this.
translations.idiomatic: Devious in conduct and false in speech, harsh at heart though humble in manner, he blocked the worthy from advancement and made all rewards and punishments serve his will.

sentences.zh: 頃以君臣之間，重於去就，冀其遷善，掩而不言。

translations.literal: Recently, between lord and minister, removal was weighed heavily; we hoped he would move toward good and covered it without speaking.
translations.idiomatic: Out of regard for the bond between ruler and minister, I had long hoped he would reform and kept silent.

sentences.zh: 曾無悔非，彌益兇戾，年序滋遠，釁惡貫盈。

translations.literal: He never repented of wrong; he grew ever more fierce and violent; years lengthened and offenses filled to the brim.
translations.idiomatic: He never repented but grew ever more vicious until his crimes overflowed.

sentences.zh: 將肅政於朝班，俾申明於憲綱，宜賜自盡。

translations.literal: We shall make government stern in the court ranks and let the law's net be declared—he should be granted suicide.
translations.idiomatic: To restore discipline at court and uphold the law, he is ordered to take his own life.

sentences.zh: 朕涉道猶淺，知人不明，理績未彰，遺闕斯眾，致茲刑辟，憫愧良深。

translations.literal: We have waded in the Way still shallowly, know men unclearly, our governing achievements not yet displayed, omissions and gaps so many—leading to this punishment; our compassionate shame is very deep.
translations.idiomatic: My grasp of governance is still shallow, my judgment of men imperfect, and my achievements few—so many failures have led to this punishment, and I am deeply ashamed.

sentences.zh: 僶俯行之，務申沮勸，凡在中外，悉朕懷焉。

translations.literal: Diligently bow and carry it out; strive to declare discouragement and encouragement—all within and without, know Our heart entirely.
translations.idiomatic: Let all within and beyond the court heed this lesson and know my mind.

sentences.zh: 」又制曰：「門下侍郎、同中書門下平章事王縉，附會奸邪，阿諛讒佞。

translations.literal: Another decree said: "Vice Director of the Chancellery and Associate Director Wang Jin attached himself to treacherous evil and fawned with flattery and slanderous sycophancy."
translations.idiomatic: A second decree stated: "Vice Director of the Chancellery and Associate Director Wang Jin attached himself to the wicked and fawned on villains."

sentences.zh: 據茲犯狀，罪至難容，矜以耋及，未忍加刑。

translations.literal: According to these offenses, guilt reaches what is hard to tolerate; pitying his advanced age, We have not borne to add punishment.
translations.idiomatic: By these offenses his guilt is grave, yet in pity for his advanced age I have not imposed capital punishment.

sentences.zh: 俾申屈法之恩，貸以嶽牧之秩。

translations.literal: Let him extend the grace of bending the law; pardon him with the rank of a mountain-and-pasture lord.
translations.idiomatic: Instead I extend the grace of leniency and grant him a provincial governorship.

sentences.zh: 可使持節括州諸軍事，守括州刺史，宜即赴任。

translations.literal: He may be made Commissioner with Credential for all military affairs of Kuo Prefecture and Defender of Kuo Prefecture; he should promptly go to his post.
translations.idiomatic: He is appointed commissioner with credential for Kuo Prefecture and prefect of Kuo, and should proceed to his post at once.

sentences.zh: 於戲！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 朕恭己南面，推誠股肱，敷求哲人，將弼予理。

translations.literal: We reverently restrain Ourselves facing south, extend sincerity to Our limbs-and-bellies, broadly seek wise men, and will have them assist Our governance.
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully face south upon the throne, entrust my ministers in good faith, and seek wise men throughout the realm to aid my rule.

sentences.zh: 昧於任使，過在朕躬，無曠厥官，各慎厥職。

translations.literal: Dark in assigning and employing men—the fault lies in Our person. Let none neglect his office; each carefully guard his duty.
translations.idiomatic: I have been blind in the appointment of men, and the fault is mine alone. Let no one neglect his post; let each heed his charge.

sentences.zh: 」初，晏等承旨，縉亦處極法，晏謂涵曰：「重刑再覆，國之常典，況誅大臣，豈得不覆奏！

translations.literal: Initially, when Yan and the others received the imperial command, Jin was also to receive the extreme penalty. Yan said to Han: "Heavy punishments require a second review—it is the state's constant rule; how much more when executing great ministers—how can one fail to submit a review memorial!
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Liu Yan and the others received the edict, Wang Jin was also sentenced to death. Yan said to Li Han, "A capital sentence must be reviewed twice—that is established law. When a great minister is to be executed, how can we not submit a review memorial!"

sentences.zh: 又法有首從，二人同刑，亦宜重取進止。

translations.literal: Moreover, the law distinguishes principal and follower; when two men share the same punishment, one should likewise earnestly seek the sovereign's final decision.
translations.idiomatic: Besides, the law distinguishes ringleader from accomplice. When two men face the same penalty, we ought all the more to seek the throne's final word.

sentences.zh: 」涵等鹹聽命。

translations.literal: Han and the others all obeyed.
translations.idiomatic: Li Han and the others all complied.

sentences.zh: 及晏等覆奏，上乃減縉罪從輕。

translations.literal: When Yan and the others submitted their review memorial, the emperor thereupon reduced Jin's crime to lighter punishment.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yan and his colleagues submitted their review, the emperor reduced Wang Jin's sentence to a lighter punishment.

sentences.zh: 載長子伯和，先是貶在揚州兵曹參軍，載得罪，命中使馳傳於揚州賜死。

translations.literal: Zai's eldest son Bohe had earlier been demoted to Military Staff Officer in Yangzhou. When Zai was found guilty, the emperor ordered an eunuch envoy to ride post-horses to Yangzhou and grant him death.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Zai's eldest son Bohe had already been demoted to military staff officer in Yangzhou. When Yuan Zai fell, the emperor dispatched an imperial messenger by post relay to Yangzhou to grant Bohe death.

sentences.zh: 次子仲武，祠部員外郎，次子季能，秘書省校書郎，並載妻王氏並賜死。

translations.literal: The second son Zhongwu was an outer-office secretary in the Sacrificial Affairs Bureau; the third son Jineng was a proofreader in the Secretariat. Together with Zai's wife Lady Wang, they were all granted death.
translations.idiomatic: The second son Zhongwu served as an outer-office secretary in the Bureau of Sacrificial Affairs; the third son Jineng was a proofreader in the Secretariat. They and Yuan Zai's wife, Lady Wang, were all ordered to take their own lives.

sentences.zh: 女資敬寺尼真一，收入掖庭。

translations.literal: The daughter Zhenyi, a nun at Zijing Temple, was taken into the Rear Palace.
translations.idiomatic: His daughter Zhenyi, a nun at Zijing Temple, was taken into the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 王氏，開元中河西節度使忠嗣之女也，素以兇戾聞，恣其子伯和等為虐。

translations.literal: Lady Wang was the daughter of Zhongsi, military governor of Hexi in the Kaiyuan era. She had long been known for fierce harshness and indulged her sons Bohe and the others in cruelty.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Wang was the daughter of Wang Zhongsi, military governor of Hexi during the Kaiyuan reign. She had long been notorious for her violent temper and allowed her sons Bohe and the others to tyrannize others at will.

sentences.zh: 伯和恃父威勢，唯以聚斂財貨，征求音樂為事。

translations.literal: Bohe relied on his father's power and prestige; his sole occupations were amassing wealth and demanding musical performers.
translations.idiomatic: Bohe traded on his father's authority, devoting himself entirely to extorting money and seizing musicians.

sentences.zh: 載在相位多年，權傾四海，外方珍異，皆集其門，資貨不可勝計，故伯和、仲武等得肆其誌。

translations.literal: Zai had held the chancellorship for many years, his power leaning over all under heaven. Exotic treasures from outside regions all gathered at his gate; goods in incalculable quantity—hence Bohe, Zhongwu, and the rest could give full vent to their desires.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Zai had held power for many years until his authority overshadowed the realm. Rare treasures from every quarter flowed to his house in sums beyond counting, and so Bohe, Zhongwu, and the rest indulged every whim.

sentences.zh: 輕浮之士，奔其門者，如恐不及。

translations.literal: Frivolous gentlemen flocking to his gate were as if fearing they could not arrive soon enough.
translations.idiomatic: Men of shallow ambition rushed to his door as though afraid of arriving too late.

sentences.zh: 名姝、異樂，禁中無者有之。

translations.literal: Celebrated beauties and exotic music—some that the palace did not have.
translations.idiomatic: Famous courtesans and exotic music—some of which not even the palace possessed.

sentences.zh: 兄弟各貯妓妾於室，倡優偎褻之戲，天倫同觀，略無愧恥。

translations.literal: The brothers each stocked rooms with courtesans and concubines. Actors and entertainers in indecent intimate plays—the whole family watched together, with hardly a shred of shame.
translations.idiomatic: Each brother kept rooms full of singing girls and concubines. Actors performed lewd entertainments while the whole family looked on together, utterly without shame.

sentences.zh: 及得罪，行路無嗟惜者。

translations.literal: When they were punished, travelers on the road spared no sigh of regret.
translations.idiomatic: When they were punished, no one on the road spared them a sigh of pity.

sentences.zh: 中使董秀、主書卓英倩、李待榮及陰陽人李季連，以載之故，皆處極法。

translations.literal: The eunuch envoy Dong Xiu, the chief clerks Zhuo Yingqian and Li Dairong, and the yin-yang master Li Jilian, on account of Zai, all received the extreme penalty.
translations.idiomatic: The palace envoy Dong Xiu, chief clerks Zhuo Yingqian and Li Dairong, and the yin-yang specialist Li Jilian were all executed on Yuan Zai's account.

sentences.zh: 遣中官於萬年縣界黃臺鄉毀載祖及父母墳墓，斫棺棄柩，及私廟木主；

translations.literal: Palace eunuchs were sent to Huangtai Township on the border of Wannian County to destroy the tombs of Zai's grandparents and parents, chop open the coffins and cast out the inner coffins, and the wooden spirit tablets of private shrines;
translations.idiomatic: Palace eunuchs were sent to Huangtai Township in Wannian County to destroy the tombs of Yuan Zai's grandparents and parents, break open the coffins and cast out the remains, and smash the spirit tablets in his private ancestral shrine;

sentences.zh: 並載大寧裏、安仁裏二宅，充修百司廨宇。

translations.literal: together with Zai's two residences in Daming Ward and Anren Ward, were all taken to repair government offices of the hundred bureaus.
translations.idiomatic: and Yuan Zai's two mansions in Daming and Anren Wards were confiscated to fund repairs to government offices throughout the capital.

sentences.zh: 以載籍沒鐘乳五百兩分賜中書門下御史臺五品已上、尚書省四品已上。

translations.literal: From Zai's confiscated register, five hundred taels of stalactite were divided and bestowed upon officials of fifth rank and above in the Chancellery, Secretariat, and Censorate, and fourth rank and above in the Ministry of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Five hundred taels of stalactite from Yuan Zai's confiscated property were divided and distributed among officials of fifth rank and above in the Chancellery, Secretariat, and Censorate, and fourth rank and above in the Ministry of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 李少良者，以吏用，早從使幕，因職遷殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: Li Shaoliang, through clerical appointment, early followed commissioners' staffs and, through his duties, was promoted to Palace Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shaoliang entered service through the clerical track, served early on commissioners' staffs, and was promoted to palace censor on account of his work.

sentences.zh: 罷，遊京師，幹謁權貴。

translations.literal: When dismissed, he traveled to the capital and sought audiences with the powerful.
translations.idiomatic: After leaving office he went to the capital and paid court to the powerful.

sentences.zh: 時元載專政，所居第宅崇侈，子弟縱橫，貨賄公行，士庶鹹嫉之。

translations.literal: At the time Yuan Zai monopolized government. His residence was grand and lavish, his sons and nephews ran rampant, bribes and gifts openly circulated—all officials and commoners alike resented it.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Yuan Zai dominated the government. His mansion was magnificent, his sons and nephews ran wild, and bribes passed openly in public view. Officials and commoners alike despised him.

sentences.zh: 少良怨不見用，乘眾怒以抗疏上聞。

translations.literal: Shaoliang, resenting that he was not employed, seized on the public anger and submitted a memorial of protest to reach the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoliang, bitter at his failure to win appointment, seized on the public outrage and submitted a memorial of protest directly to the throne.

sentences.zh: 留少良於禁內客省，少良友人韋頌因至禁門訪少良，少良漏其言；

translations.literal: Shaoliang was detained in the Inner Palace Guest Office. His friend Wei Song came to the Forbidden Gate to visit Shaoliang, and Shaoliang leaked his words;
translations.idiomatic: Shaoliang was held in the inner palace guest quarters. His friend Wei Song came to the palace gate to visit him, and Shaoliang let slip what he had said;

sentences.zh: 頌不慎密，遂為載備知之，乃奏少良狂妄，詔下御史臺訊鞫。

translations.literal: Song was not careful with secrecy, and so Zai came to know it fully. He then memorialized that Shaoliang was reckless and insubordinate, and an edict was issued ordering the Censorate to interrogate.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Song failed to keep the matter secret, and Yuan Zai learned everything. Yuan Zai then memorialized that Shaoliang was insolent and reckless, and an edict ordered the Censorate to investigate.

sentences.zh: 是時御史大夫缺，載以張延賞為之，屬意焉。

translations.literal: At that time the post of Censor-in-Chief was vacant. Zai appointed Zhang Yanshang to it and put his hopes in him.
translations.idiomatic: The post of censor-in-chief was then vacant, and Yuan Zai appointed Zhang Yanshang to it, counting on his cooperation.

sentences.zh: 少良以泄禁中奏議，制使陸珽同伏罪。

translations.literal: Shaoliang, for leaking memorials and deliberations within the Forbidden Palace, and Commissioner Lu Ting—together they were found guilty.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoliang was convicted of leaking memorials and deliberations from within the palace; the imperial commissioner Lu Ting was condemned along with him.

sentences.zh: 初，韋頌及珽俱與少良友善，與載子弟親黨款狎。

translations.literal: Initially, Wei Song and Lu Ting were both friendly with Shaoliang and were on familiar, intimate terms with Zai's sons, nephews, and close associates.
translations.idiomatic: At first Wei Song and Lu Ting had both been on friendly terms with Shaoliang and were intimate with Yuan Zai's sons, nephews, and close associates.

sentences.zh: 頌得少良微旨，漏於載所親，遂達於載。

translations.literal: Song got Shaoliang's subtle intent and leaked it to Zai's intimates, and it thus reached Zai.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Song grasped Shaoliang's meaning and passed word of it to Yuan Zai's confidants, and so it reached Yuan Zai.

sentences.zh: 載密召珽問之，珽具白其狀及禁中語。

translations.literal: Zai secretly summoned Lu Ting to question him. Ting fully reported the circumstances and the words spoken within the Forbidden Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Zai secretly summoned Lu Ting and questioned him. Ting told him everything, including what had been said inside the palace.

sentences.zh: 載得之，奏於上前，上大怒，並付京兆府決殺。

translations.literal: Zai obtained this and memorialized it before the emperor. The emperor was greatly enraged and handed them all over to the Capital Prefecture for summary execution.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Zai reported this to the emperor, who flew into a rage and ordered all of them handed over to the capital prefecture for execution.

sentences.zh: 珽，國子司業善經之子也，少傳父業，頗通經史，性浮躁而疏，故及於累。

translations.literal: Lu Ting was the son of Guozi Vice Director Shanjing. In youth he inherited his father's learning, was fairly versed in classics and histories, but by nature was impulsive and careless—hence he came to ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Ting was the son of Shanjing, vice director of the Directorate of Education. In youth he had inherited his father's scholarship and was fairly learned in the classics and histories, but he was rash and careless by nature—and so came to ruin.

sentences.zh: 大歷中，元載弄權自恣，人皆惡之。

translations.literal: In the Dali era, Yuan Zai manipulated power as he pleased; everyone hated him.
translations.idiomatic: During the Dali reign, Yuan Zai wielded power as he pleased, and everyone loathed him.

sentences.zh: 八年七月，晉州男子郇謨以麻辮發，持竹筐及葦席哭於東市。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of year 8, the man Huan Mo of Jin Prefecture, with hemp braids for hair, holding a bamboo basket and reed mat, wept at the Eastern Market.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of Dali 8, 773, a commoner of Jin Prefecture named Huan Mo, his hair bound in hemp braids, carrying a bamboo basket and a reed mat, wept at the Eastern Market.

sentences.zh: 人問其故，對曰：「有三十字請獻於上。

translations.literal: People asked the reason. He replied: "I have thirty characters to present to the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: When people asked why, he answered, "I have thirty characters to present to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 若無堪，便以竹筐貯屍，棄之於野。

translations.literal: If they are not acceptable, then use the bamboo basket to hold my corpse and cast it in the wilds.
translations.idiomatic: If they are not accepted, let this basket hold my corpse and cast it in the wilderness."

sentences.zh: 」京兆府以聞。

translations.literal: The Capital Prefecture reported it.
translations.idiomatic: The capital prefecture reported the matter.

sentences.zh: 上既召見，賜衣，館於禁內客省。

translations.literal: Once the emperor had summoned and received him, he granted him clothing and housed him in the Inner Palace Guest Office.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned and received him, granted him clothing, and lodged him in the inner palace guest quarters.

sentences.zh: 其獻三十字，各論一事。

translations.literal: The thirty characters he presented each discussed one matter.
translations.idiomatic: The thirty characters he submitted each addressed a separate issue.

sentences.zh: 其要者：「團」字、「監」字。

translations.literal: The important ones were the character "Regiment" and the character "Supervisor."
translations.idiomatic: The crucial ones were the characters for "regiment" and "supervisor."

sentences.zh: 團者，請罷諸州團練使；

translations.literal: "Regiment" meant requesting abolition of the regimental trainers in all prefectures;
translations.idiomatic: "Regiment" called for abolishing the regimental training commissioners in every prefecture;

sentences.zh: 監者，請罷諸道監軍使。

translations.literal: "Supervisor" meant requesting abolition of the army supervisors in all circuits.
translations.idiomatic: "Supervisor" called for abolishing the army supervisors in every circuit.

sentences.zh: 殿中御史楊護職居左巡，郇謨哭市，護不聞奏，上以為蔽匿，貶連州桂陽縣丞員外置。

translations.literal: Palace Censor Yang Hu held the left patrol duty. Huan Mo wept at the market, but Hu did not hear and memorialize. The emperor considered this concealment and demoted him to Supplementary Assistant Magistrate of Guiyang County in Lian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Palace censor Yang Hu held the left patrol post. Huan Mo wept in the market, yet Hu failed to hear of it and report it. The emperor took this for deliberate concealment and demoted him to supplementary assistant magistrate of Guiyang County in Lian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 元載當承寵得誌，每改張朝政，出於載手，中外共怒，當時歸咎於載，故少良封事於前，郇謨哭市於後。

translations.literal: Yuan Zai, enjoying favor and getting his way, altered and reshaped court governance with every change—all emanating from Zai's hand. Within and without shared the anger, and at the time blame was laid on Zai. Hence Shaoliang's sealed memorial came first and Huan Mo's market weeping after.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Zai, secure in imperial favor, reshaped court policy at will, and every change issued from his hand. Court and country alike were enraged, and blame at the time fell on Yuan Zai—hence Li Shaoliang's sealed memorial came first, and Huan Mo's weeping at the market followed.

sentences.zh: 凡百有位，宜為明誡。

translations.literal: All who hold offices should take this as a clear warning.
translations.idiomatic: Let all who hold office take this as a plain warning.

sentences.zh: 王縉，字夏卿，河中人也。

translations.literal: Wang Jin, courtesy name Xiaqing, was a native of Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jin, courtesy name Xiaqing, was a native of Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 少好學，與兄維早以文翰著名。

translations.literal: In youth he loved learning. With his elder brother Wei he was early famous for literary brushwork.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he loved learning. He and his elder brother Wang Wei won early fame for their literary gifts.

sentences.zh: 縉連應草澤及文辭清麗舉，累授侍御史、武部員外。

translations.literal: Jin passed in succession the Recluse of Grasslands and Clear Literary Style examinations and was repeatedly appointed Supervising Censor and Vice Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jin passed the Recluse of the Grasslands and Clear Literary Style examinations in succession and rose through appointments as supervising censor and vice director of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 祿山之亂，選為太原少尹，與李光弼同守太原，功效謀略，眾所推先，加憲部侍郎，兼本官。

translations.literal: During the An Lushan rebellion he was selected as Vice Director of Taiyuan and with Li Guangbi jointly defended Taiyuan. In merit, effect, and strategy he was ranked first by all, and was promoted to Vice Director of the Bureau of Justice while retaining his original post.
translations.idiomatic: During the An Lushan rebellion he was chosen as vice director of Taiyuan and, together with Li Guangbi, held the city. For achievement, effect, and strategy he was ranked above all others, and was promoted to vice director of the Bureau of Justice while retaining his existing post.

sentences.zh: 時兄維陷賊，受偽署，賊平，維付吏議，縉請以己官贖維之罪，特為減等。

translations.literal: At the time his elder brother Wei had fallen into rebel hands and accepted a false appointment. When the rebels were pacified, Wei was handed over to officials for judgment. Jin requested to redeem Wei's crime with his own rank, and was specially granted a reduction of punishment grade.
translations.idiomatic: At that time his elder brother Wang Wei had fallen into rebel hands and accepted a false appointment. After the rebellion was crushed, Wei was handed over for judgment. Wang Jin asked to redeem his brother's guilt with his own rank, and the court specially reduced Wei's sentence by one grade.

sentences.zh: 縉尋入拜國子祭酒，改鳳翔尹、秦隴州防禦使，歷工部侍郎、左散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Jin soon entered the capital and was appointed Chancellor of the Directorate of Education. He was transferred to Magistrate of Fengxiang and Defender of Qin-Long Prefecture, and served successively as Vice Director of the Bureau of Works and Left Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jin soon entered court and was appointed chancellor of the Directorate of Education. He then served as magistrate of Fengxiang and defender of Qin-Long Prefecture, and later as vice director of the Bureau of Works and left regular attendant.

sentences.zh: 撰《玄宗哀冊文》，時稱為工。

translations.literal: He composed the "Lament for Emperor Xuanzong," which at the time was praised as well crafted.
translations.idiomatic: He composed the Lament for Emperor Xuanzong, which contemporaries praised as a masterly piece of writing.

sentences.zh: 改兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to vice director of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 屬平殄史朝義，河朔未安，詔縉以本官河北宣慰，奉使稱旨。

translations.literal: When Shih Chaoyi was fully destroyed but Hebei remained unsettled, an edict appointed Jin in his current office as Pacification Commissioner of Hebei. His mission accorded with the imperial will.
translations.idiomatic: After Shi Chaoyi was destroyed but Hebei remained unsettled, an edict appointed Wang Jin, in his existing office, pacification commissioner of Hebei. His mission pleased the throne.

sentences.zh: 廣德二年，拜黃門侍郎、同平章事、太微宮使、弘文崇賢館大學士。

translations.literal: In Guangde 2 he was appointed Vice Director of the Yellow Gate, Associate Director of the Chancellery, Commissioner of the Twei Palace, and Grand Academician of the Hongwen and Chongxian Institutes.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangde 2, 764, he was appointed vice director of the Yellow Gate, associate director of the Chancellery, commissioner of the Twei Palace, and grand academician of the Hongwen and Chongxian Institutes.

sentences.zh: 其年，河南副元帥李光弼薨於徐州，以縉為侍中、持節都統河南、淮西、山南東道諸節度行營事。

translations.literal: That same year, Vice Commander-in-Chief Li Guangbi died at Xuzhou. Jin was made Minister of the Palace Secretariat, with credential to command overall the military camps of the circuits of Henan, Huaixi, and Shannan East.
translations.idiomatic: That same year Vice Commander-in-Chief Li Guangbi died at Xuzhou. Wang Jin was made minister of the Palace Secretariat and, bearing the imperial credential, given overall command of the Henan, Huaixi, and Shannan East military circuits.

sentences.zh: 縉懇讓侍中，從之，加上柱國，兼東都留守。

translations.literal: Jin earnestly declined the Ministry of the Palace Secretariat, and his request was granted. He was given the title Exalted Pillar of State and concurrently made Eastern Capital Intendant.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jin earnestly declined the post of minister of the Palace Secretariat, and the emperor agreed. He was given the title Exalted Pillar of State and made concurrently eastern capital intendant.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，遷河南副元帥，請減軍資錢四十萬貫修東都殿宇。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was promoted to Vice Commander-in-Chief of Henan and requested to reduce military funds by four hundred thousand strings of cash to repair the Eastern Capital's palaces and halls.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year he was promoted to vice commander-in-chief of Henan and requested that four hundred thousand strings of military funds be diverted to repair the palaces of the eastern capital.

sentences.zh: 大歷三年，幽州節度使李懷仙死，以縉領幽州、盧龍節度。

translations.literal: In Dali 3, Military Governor Li Huaixian of You Prefecture died. Jin was put in charge of You Prefecture and Lulong Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In Dali 3, 768, Military Governor Li Huaixian of Youzhou died, and Wang Jin was put in charge of Youzhou and the Lulong circuit.

sentences.zh: 縉赴鎮而還，委政於燕將硃希彩。

translations.literal: Jin went to the garrison and returned, entrusting government to the Yan general Zhu Xicai.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jin went to the garrison and then returned, leaving affairs in the hands of the Yan general Zhu Xicai.

sentences.zh: 又屬河東節度辛雲京卒，遂兼太原尹、北都留守、河東節度營田觀察等使。

translations.literal: When Military Governor Xin Yunjing of Hedong also died, Jin concurrently became Magistrate of Taiyuan, Northern Capital Intendant, and Military Governor, Garrison-Farming Commissioner, and Surveillance Commissioner of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: When Hedong military governor Xin Yunjing also died, Wang Jin added the posts of magistrate of Taiyuan, northern capital intendant, and military governor, garrison-farming commissioner, and surveillance commissioner of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 縉又讓河南副元帥、東都留守，從之。

translations.literal: Jin again declined the posts of Vice Commander-in-Chief of Henan and Eastern Capital Intendant, and his request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jin again declined the posts of vice commander-in-chief of Henan and eastern capital intendant, and the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 太原舊將王無縱、張奉璋等恃功，且以縉儒者易之，每事多違約束。

translations.literal: Old generals of Taiyuan, Wang Wuzong and Zhang Fengzhang and the rest, relying on past merit and moreover taking Jin, a Confucian scholar, as easy to handle, in many matters violated his orders.
translations.idiomatic: The old Taiyuan generals Wang Wuzong, Zhang Fengzhang, and others, trusting in past merit and taking Wang Jin, a scholar-official, to be easy to manage, repeatedly defied his orders.

sentences.zh: 縉一朝悉召斬之，將校股栗。

translations.literal: Jin one morning summoned them all and executed them. Officers and commanders trembled in their thighs.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jin summoned them all one morning and had them executed. Officers and commanders trembled with fear.

sentences.zh: 二歲，罷河東歸朝，授門下侍郎、中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: After two years he was removed from Hedong and returned to court, appointed Vice Director of the Gate and Associate Director of the Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: After two years he was relieved of his Hedong command and recalled to court, appointed vice director of the Gate and associate director of the Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 時元載用事，縉卑附之，不敢與忤，然恃才與老，多所傲忽。

translations.literal: At the time Yuan Zai was in power. Jin humbly attached himself and did not dare oppose him, yet relying on talent and age he was often haughty and neglectful toward others.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Yuan Zai held power. Wang Jin fawned on him and did not dare oppose him, yet relying on his talent and seniority he often treated others with arrogance and disdain.

sentences.zh: 載所不悅，心雖希載旨，然以言辭淩詬，無所忌憚。

translations.literal: When displeased, even though in heart he courted Zai's intent, in words he would insult and revile without restraint or fear.
translations.idiomatic: Even toward those Yuan Zai disliked, though in his heart he sought to please Yuan Zai, in speech he insulted and abused them without restraint.

sentences.zh: 時京兆尹黎幹者，戎州人也，數論事，載甚病之，而力不能去也。

translations.literal: At the time the Capital Prefect Li Gan was a native of Rong Prefecture. He often discussed affairs in council, which greatly troubled Zai, yet Zai lacked the power to remove him.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the capital prefect Li Gan was a native of Rongzhou. He often spoke up in council, which greatly vexed Yuan Zai, yet Yuan Zai lacked the power to remove him.

sentences.zh: 幹嘗白事於縉，縉曰：「尹，南方君子也，安知朝禮！

translations.literal: Gan once reported business to Jin. Jin said: "Prefect, you are a gentleman of the south—how would you know court ritual!
translations.idiomatic: Li Gan once reported business to Wang Jin. Jin said, "Prefect, you are a gentleman of the south—what would you know of court ritual!"

sentences.zh: 」其慢而侮人，率如此類。

translations.literal: His contempt and insult toward others were generally of this sort.
translations.idiomatic: His contempt and insults were generally of this sort.

sentences.zh: 縉弟兄奉佛，不茹葷血，縉晚年尤甚。

translations.literal: Jin and his brothers observed Buddhism and ate no meat or blood. Jin in his later years was especially strict.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jin and his brothers practiced Buddhism and ate no meat. Wang Jin became especially strict in his later years.

sentences.zh: 與杜鴻漸舍財造寺無限極。

translations.literal: With Du Hongjian he spent wealth building temples without limit.
translations.idiomatic: Together with Du Hongjian he spent limitless sums building temples.

sentences.zh: 妻李氏卒，舍道政裏第為寺，為之追福，奏其額曰寶應，度僧三十人住持。

translations.literal: When his wife Lady Li died, he donated his residence in Daozheng Ward as a temple to obtain merit for her soul. He memorialized that its plaque be named Baoying and ordained thirty monks to serve as abbots.
translations.idiomatic: When his wife Lady Li died, he converted his mansion in Daozheng Ward into a temple to gain merit for her soul. He memorialized that it be named Baoying Temple and ordained thirty monks to serve as its clergy.

sentences.zh: 每節度觀察使入朝，必延至寶應寺，諷令施財，助己修繕。

translations.literal: Whenever military and surveillance commissioners came to court, he invariably invited them to Baoying Temple and hinted that they donate funds to assist his own repairs.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever military and surveillance commissioners came to court, he always invited them to Baoying Temple and hinted that they should donate funds toward his own repairs.

sentences.zh: 初，代宗喜祠祀，未甚重佛，而元載、杜鴻漸與縉喜飯僧徒。

translations.literal: Initially Emperor Daizong favored sacrificial rites and did not yet greatly esteem Buddhism, yet Yuan Zai, Du Hongjian, and Jin delighted in entertaining monks.
translations.idiomatic: At first Emperor Daizong favored state sacrifices and did not greatly esteem Buddhism, yet Yuan Zai, Du Hongjian, and Wang Jin delighted in feasting monks.

sentences.zh: 代宗嘗問以福業報應事，載等因而啟奏，代宗由是奉之過當，嘗令僧百余人於宮中陳設佛像，經行念誦，謂之內道場。

translations.literal: Emperor Daizong once inquired about karmic merit and retribution. Zai and the others thereupon submitted memorials on it, and Daizong from this honored it excessively. He once ordered more than a hundred monks to set up Buddha images within the palace, walk in procession and chant sutras—called the Inner Way-Altar.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Daizong once asked about karmic merit and retribution. Yuan Zai and the others seized the opening to memorialized on the subject, and from that point Daizong honored Buddhism excessively. He once ordered more than a hundred monks to install Buddha images in the palace, walk in procession, and chant sutras in what was called the Inner Way-Altar.

sentences.zh: 其飲膳之厚，窮極珍異，出入乘廄焉，度支具廩給。

translations.literal: The thickness of their food and drink reached the utmost in rare delicacies. Going in and out they rode stable horses, and the Department of Revenue supplied full provisions.
translations.idiomatic: Their fare was lavish beyond measure, with the rarest delicacies. They rode palace horses when entering and leaving, and the Department of Revenue supplied their full rations.

sentences.zh: 每西蕃入寇，必令群僧講誦《仁王經》，以攘虜寇。

translations.literal: Whenever the Western Tibetans raided, he invariably ordered the assembly of monks to expound and recite the Humane Kings Sutra to repel the barbarian invaders.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the Tibetans raided from the west, he invariably ordered monks assembled to expound and recite the Humane Kings Sutra to drive off the invaders.

sentences.zh: 茍幸其退，則橫加錫賜。

translations.literal: If by chance they withdrew, lavish rewards were heaped upon them.
translations.idiomatic: If the enemy happened to withdraw, lavish rewards were heaped upon the monks.

sentences.zh: 胡僧不空，官至卿監，封國公，通籍禁中，勢移公卿，爭權擅威，日相淩奪。

translations.literal: The foreign monk Amoghavajra reached ministerial and supervisory offices, was enfeoffed as Duke of a State, had access to the Forbidden Palace registers, his power swayed the high ministers—contending for power and arrogating authority, daily encroaching on one another.
translations.idiomatic: The foreign monk Amoghavajra rose to ministerial and supervisory rank, was enfeoffed as duke of a state, and gained access to the inner palace. His power eclipsed that of the chief ministers; he and his rivals contended for authority and daily encroached on one another.

sentences.zh: 凡京畿之豐田美利，多歸於寺觀，吏不能制。

translations.literal: All the fertile fields and profitable resources of the capital region largely passed to temples and monasteries, and officials could not control it.
translations.idiomatic: The fertile fields and profitable holdings of the capital region largely passed into the hands of temples and monasteries, and officials could not restrain them.

sentences.zh: 僧之徒侶，雖有贓奸畜亂，敗戮相繼，而代宗信心不易，乃詔天下官吏不得箠曳僧尼。

translations.literal: Among the monks' companions, though corruption, wickedness, and disorder accumulated, defeat and execution following one after another, Daizong's faith did not change. He then decreed that officials throughout the realm must not beat or drag monks and nuns.
translations.idiomatic: Though monks and their followers piled up corruption, wickedness, and disorder, and defeat and execution followed one after another, Daizong's faith did not waver. He decreed that officials throughout the realm must not beat or drag monks and nuns.

sentences.zh: 又見縉等施財立寺，窮極瑰麗，每對揚啟沃，必以業果為證。

translations.literal: Moreover, seeing Jin and the others spend wealth to erect temples of utmost splendor, whenever they faced the emperor and offered counsel they invariably used karmic cause and fruit as proof.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, seeing Wang Jin and the others spend fortunes on temples of surpassing splendor, whenever they addressed the emperor they invariably cited karmic cause and fruit as proof.

sentences.zh: 以為國家慶祚靈長，皆福報所資，業力已定，雖小有患難，不足道也。

translations.literal: They held that the state's blessed reign and spiritual endurance all depended on rewards of merit; once karmic force was fixed, even minor calamities were not worth mentioning.
translations.idiomatic: They held that the dynasty's long fortune and enduring mandate all rested on the fruits of merit; once karmic destiny was fixed, even minor disasters were not worth mentioning.

sentences.zh: 故祿山、思明毒亂方熾，而皆有子禍。

translations.literal: Hence when An Lushan and Shi Siming's poisonous rebellions were still raging, both suffered ruin through their sons.
translations.idiomatic: Thus when the rebellions of An Lushan and Shi Siming were still raging, both were destroyed through their sons.

sentences.zh: 仆固懷恩將亂而死；

translations.literal: Pugu Huai'en was about to rebel when he died;
translations.idiomatic: Pugu Huai'en was on the verge of rebellion when he died;

sentences.zh: 西戎犯闕，未擊而退。

translations.literal: the Western barbarians violated the capital and withdrew without being struck.
translations.idiomatic: the western barbarians reached the capital and withdrew without being attacked.

sentences.zh: 此皆非人事之明征也。

translations.literal: These were all not clear evidence from human affairs.
translations.idiomatic: None of this, they claimed, was clear proof from the realm of human affairs.

sentences.zh: 帝信之愈甚。

translations.literal: The emperor believed it ever more deeply.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor believed it all the more deeply.

sentences.zh: 公卿大臣既掛以業報，則人事棄而不修，故大歷刑政，日以陵遲，有由然也。

translations.literal: Once grand ministers and great officials were hung up on karmic retribution, human affairs were abandoned and not attended to. Hence in the Dali era punishments and government daily declined; there was cause for it.
translations.idiomatic: Once ministers and high officials were preoccupied with karmic retribution, human governance was neglected. Thus under the Dali reign law and administration daily declined—and there was reason for it.

sentences.zh: 五臺山有金閣寺，鑄銅為瓦，塗金於上，照耀山谷，計錢巨億萬。

translations.literal: On Mount Wutai was Jinge Temple. Copper was cast into tiles and gilded on top, shining across the valleys—the cost reckoned at hundreds of millions.
translations.idiomatic: On Mount Wutai stood Jinge Temple, its roof tiles cast in copper and gilded until they blazed across the valleys. The cost was reckoned in the hundreds of millions.

sentences.zh: 縉為宰相，給中書符牒，令臺山僧數十人分行郡縣，聚徒講說，以求貨利。

translations.literal: When Jin was chancellor, he issued chancery credentials and orders, sending several dozen Mount Wutai monks to travel through prefectures and counties, gathering congregations to preach and lecture, seeking profit.
translations.idiomatic: While Wang Jin was chancellor, he issued chancery credentials dispatching several dozen Mount Wutai monks to travel through prefectures and counties, gathering crowds to preach and lecture in pursuit of profit.

sentences.zh: 代宗七月望日於內道場造盂蘭盆，飾以金翠，所費百萬。

translations.literal: On the fifteenth of the seventh month Emperor Daizong made a Ullambana offering in the Inner Way-Altar, adorned with gold and kingfisher feather inlay—costing a million.
translations.idiomatic: On the fifteenth day of the seventh month Emperor Daizong made an Ullambana offering in the Inner Way-Altar, adorned with gold and kingfisher inlay at a cost of a million cash.

sentences.zh: 又設高祖已下七聖神座，備幡節、龍傘、衣裳之制，各書尊號於幡上以識之，舁出內，陳於寺觀。

translations.literal: He also set up spirit seats for the Seven Sages from Gaozu downward, complete with banners, insignia, dragon umbrellas, and vestments. Each had imperial honorific titles written on banners for identification. They were borne out of the Inner Palace and displayed at temples and monasteries.
translations.idiomatic: He also set up spirit seats for the Seven Sages from Emperor Gaozu downward, complete with banners, insignia, dragon umbrellas, and ceremonial robes. Each banner bore an imperial honorific title for identification. They were carried out of the inner palace and displayed at temples and monasteries.

sentences.zh: 是日，排儀仗，百僚序立於光順門以俟之，幡花鼓舞，迎呼道路。

translations.literal: That day formations of ceremonial guards were drawn up. The hundred officials lined up in order at Guangshun Gate to await them—banners, flowers, drums and dance, greeting and shouting along the roads.
translations.idiomatic: That day ceremonial guards were drawn up in formation. The hundred officials lined up at Guangshun Gate to await the procession—banners and flowers, drums and dancers, with crowds cheering along the roads.

sentences.zh: 歲以為常，而識者嗤其不典，其傷教之源始於縉也。

translations.literal: Year after year this became custom, but knowing men mocked it as uncanonical—the source of injury to the teaching began with Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Year after year this became custom, but men of discernment mocked it as a breach of propriety. The source of injury to the faith began with Wang Jin.

sentences.zh: 李氏，初為左丞韋濟妻，濟卒，奔縉。

translations.literal: Lady Li was at first wife of Vice Director Wei Ji. When Ji died, she fled to Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Li had first been the wife of Vice Director Wei Ji. When Ji died, she went to Wang Jin.

sentences.zh: 縉嬖之，冒稱為妻，實妾也。

translations.literal: Jin favored her and falsely claimed her as wife—she was in fact a concubine.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jin favored her and falsely presented her as his wife—she was in fact a concubine.

sentences.zh: 又縱弟妹女尼等廣納財賄，貪猥之跡如市賈焉。

translations.literal: Moreover he indulged his younger siblings and nuns to widely accept bribes; traces of greed and vulgarity were like a market merchant.
translations.idiomatic: He also allowed his siblings and the nuns in his household to take bribes on a wide scale, and his greed and grasping ways were those of a market hawker.

sentences.zh: 元載得罪，縉連坐貶括州刺史，移處州刺史。

translations.literal: When Yuan Zai fell from power, Jin was implicated and demoted to Prefect of Kuozhou, then transferred to Prefect of Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Zai was condemned, Wang Jin was implicated and demoted to prefect of Kuozhou, then reassigned as prefect of Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 大歷十四年，除太子賓客，留司東都。

translations.literal: In Dali 14, he was appointed Guest of the Heir Apparent and remained on duty at the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: In Dali 14, 779, he was appointed guest of the heir apparent and remained on duty at the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 建中二年十二月卒，年八十二。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of Jianzhong 2 he died, aged eighty-two.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the twelfth month of Jianzhong 2, 781, at the age of eighty-two.

sentences.zh: 楊炎，字公南，鳳翔人。

translations.literal: Yang Yan, courtesy name Gongnan, was a native of Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yan, courtesy name Gongnan, came from Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 曾祖大寶，武德初為龍門令，劉武周陷晉、絳，攻之不降，城破被害，褒贈全節侯。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Dabao, in the early Wude era, served as Magistrate of Longmen. When Liu Wuzhou seized Jin and Jiang, he attacked but would not submit; when the city fell he was killed, and posthumously enfeoffed as Marquis of Quanjie.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Dabao, in the early Wude reign, served as magistrate of Longmen. When Liu Wuzhou seized Jin and Jiang and attacked the city, Dabao refused to surrender; when the city fell he was killed, and the court posthumously enfeoffed him as Marquis of Quanjie for his integrity unto death.

sentences.zh: 祖哲，以孝行有異，旌其門閭。

translations.literal: His grandfather Zhe, for extraordinary filial conduct, had his gate and neighborhood honored.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Zhe, for exceptional filial conduct, had an honor arch erected at his gate.

sentences.zh: 父播，登進士第，隱居不仕，玄宗征為諫議大夫，棄官就養，亦以孝行禎祥，表其門閭。

translations.literal: His father Bo passed the jinshi examination, lived in seclusion without taking office. Xuanzong summoned him as Remonstrance Official; he abandoned his post to go care for his parents, and for filial conduct and auspicious omens his gate and neighborhood were likewise honored.
translations.idiomatic: His father Bo passed the jinshi examination and lived in retirement without taking office. Emperor Xuanzong summoned him as remonstrance official, but he resigned to care for his parents at home. For his filial devotion and the auspicious omens that attended it, his gate was honored in the same way.

sentences.zh: 肅宗就加散騎常侍，賜號玄靖先生，名在《逸人傳》。

translations.literal: Suzong then additionally made him Regular Attendant of the Chariots and Horses, bestowed the title Master Xuanjing, and listed his name in 《Record of Recluses》.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Suzong then further appointed him regular attendant of the chariots and horses, granted him the title Master Xuanjing, and entered his name in 《Record of Recluses》.

sentences.zh: 炎美須眉，風骨峻峙，文藻雄麗，汧、隴之間，號為小楊山人。

translations.literal: Yan had handsome eyebrows and beard, stern bearing, and magnificent literary style; between Qian and Long he was known as the Lesser Recluse of Yang.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yan had striking features and a commanding presence, and his writing was bold and splendid. Between Qian and Long he was known as the Lesser Recluse of Yang.
