sentences.zh: 釋褐辟河西節度掌書記。

translations.literal: Upon first taking office he was appointed secretary to the Hexi military governor.
translations.idiomatic: On entering official life he was appointed secretary to the military governor of Hexi.

sentences.zh: 神烏令李大簡嘗因醉辱炎，至是與炎同幕，率左右反接之，鐵棒撾之二百，流血被地，幾死。

translations.literal: Shenwu Magistrate Li Dajian had once insulted Yan while drunk. Now serving on the same staff, Yan gathered attendants, bound him with hands behind his back, and beat him two hundred blows with an iron rod—blood soaked the ground and he nearly died.
translations.idiomatic: Li Dajian, magistrate of Shenwu, had once humiliated Yang Yan while drunk. When they now served on the same staff, Yan had his attendants seize Dajian, bind his arms behind him, and beat him two hundred times with an iron rod until blood pooled on the ground and he nearly died.

sentences.zh: 節度使呂崇賁愛其才，不之責。

translations.literal: Military Governor Lü Chongben valued his talent and did not punish him.
translations.idiomatic: Military Governor Lü Chongben admired his ability and did not hold him accountable.

sentences.zh: 後副元帥李光弼奏為判官，不應，征拜起居舍人，辭祿就養岐下。

translations.literal: Later Vice Commander Li Guangbi recommended him as aide; he declined. Summoned as Attendant for Daily Affairs, he declined salary to go care for his parents at Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Later Vice Commander-in-Chief Li Guangbi recommended him as aide, but he refused. When summoned as attendant for daily affairs, he declined the salary and returned to Qi to support his parents.

sentences.zh: 丁憂，廬於墓前，號泣不絕聲，有紫芝白雀之祥，又表其門閭。

translations.literal: On entering mourning he built a hut before the tomb and wept without cease; auspicious purple fungus and white sparrows appeared, and his gate and neighborhood were honored once again.
translations.idiomatic: During mourning he built a hut by the grave and wept without stopping. Purple fungus and white sparrows appeared as auspicious signs, and once again an honor arch was raised at his gate.

sentences.zh: 孝著三代，門樹六闕，古未有也。

translations.literal: Filial piety distinguished across three generations, six honor arches at the gate—unprecedented in antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Filial devotion had marked three generations of the family, and six honor arches stood at their gate—something without precedent in antiquity.

sentences.zh: 服闋久之，起為司勛員外郎，改兵部，轉禮部郎中、知制誥。

translations.literal: Long after mourning ended he was recalled as Vice Director in the Bureau of Merit, transferred to the Ministry of War, then promoted to Director in the Ministry of Rites with oversight of edicts.
translations.idiomatic: Long after his mourning ended he was recalled as vice director in the Bureau of Merit, moved to the Ministry of War, and then promoted to director in the Ministry of Rites with responsibility for drafting edicts.

sentences.zh: 遷中書舍人，與常袞並掌綸誥，袞長於除書，炎善為德音，自開元已來，言詔制之美者，時稱常、楊焉。

translations.literal: Promoted to Secretariat Drafting Officer; with Chang Gun he jointly managed imperial edicts. Gun excelled at appointment documents, Yan at gracious proclamations. Since Kaiyuan, in speaking of fine edict-drafting, the age called them Chang and Yang.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to secretariat drafting officer and, together with Chang Gun, handled imperial edicts. Gun excelled at appointment documents, while Yan excelled at gracious proclamations. Since the Kaiyuan era, whenever people spoke of fine edict-drafting, they named Chang and Yang.

sentences.zh: 炎樂賢下士，以汲引為己任，人士歸之。

translations.literal: Yan delighted in honoring the worthy and deferring to scholars, taking advancement of talent as his charge; men of letters gathered to him.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yan loved to honor the worthy and treat scholars with respect, making the advancement of talent his personal mission, and men of letters flocked to him.

sentences.zh: 嘗為《李楷洛碑》，辭甚工，文士莫不成誦之。

translations.literal: He once composed 《Stele for Li Kaoluo》, the wording extremely fine; literary men all memorized and recited it.
translations.idiomatic: He once wrote 《Stele for Li Kaoluo》, a piece of extraordinary craftsmanship that literary men memorized and recited by heart.

sentences.zh: 遷吏部侍郎，修國史。

translations.literal: Promoted to Vice Minister of Personnel; he compiled the national history.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice minister of personnel and worked on the national history.

sentences.zh: 元載自作相，常選擢朝士有文學才望者一人厚遇之，將以代己。

translations.literal: When Yuan Zai himself became chancellor, he regularly selected one court official of literary talent and reputation for lavish favor, intending him to replace himself.
translations.idiomatic: Once Yuan Zai became chancellor himself, he regularly singled out one court official of literary talent and reputation for special favor, intending to groom him as his successor.

sentences.zh: 初，引禮部郎中劉單；

translations.literal: At first he brought forward Director Liu Dan of the Ministry of Rites;
translations.idiomatic: At first he brought forward Liu Dan, director in the Ministry of Rites;

sentences.zh: 單卒，引吏部侍郎薛邕，邕貶，又引炎。

translations.literal: When Dan died, he brought forward Vice Minister Xue Yong of Personnel; when Yong was demoted, he brought forward Yan.
translations.idiomatic: when Liu Dan died, he brought forward Xue Yong, vice minister of personnel; when Xue was demoted, he brought forward Yang Yan.

sentences.zh: 載親重炎，無與為比。

translations.literal: Zai cherished and esteemed Yan—no one could compare.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Zai favored Yang Yan above all others; no one could compare.

sentences.zh: 載敗，坐貶道州司馬。

translations.literal: When Zai fell, Yan was implicated and demoted to military adjutant of Daozhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Zai fell, Yang Yan was implicated and demoted to military adjutant of Daozhou.

sentences.zh: 德宗即位，議用宰相，崔祐甫薦炎有文學器用，上亦自聞其名，拜銀青光祿大夫、門下侍郎、同平章事。

translations.literal: When Dezong took the throne, they discussed appointing chancellors. Cui Youfu recommended Yan for literary talent and capacity; the emperor had also heard his name, and appointed him Honorary Grand Master of the Brilliant Hall with Golden Seal, Vice Director of the Chancellery, and Associate Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Dezong acceded, the court debated whom to appoint chancellor. Cui Youfu recommended Yang Yan for his literary gifts and practical ability, and the emperor had already heard his name. Yan was appointed honorary grand master of the Brilliant Hall with golden seal, vice director of the chancellery, and associate director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 炎有風儀，博以文學，早負時稱，天下翕然，望為賢相。

translations.literal: Yan had dignified bearing, broad literary learning, and early commanded fame of the age; all under Heaven turned toward him, expecting a worthy chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yan had presence and erudition, and had long enjoyed a fine reputation. All under Heaven looked to him with hope that he would prove a worthy chancellor.

sentences.zh: 初，國家舊制，天下財賦皆納於左藏庫，而太府四時以數聞，尚書比部覆其出入，上下相轄，無失遺。

translations.literal: Originally, under the state's old system, all revenue and levies under Heaven were deposited in the Left Storehouse Treasury; the Grand Treasury reported figures each season, and the Ministry of Revenue's Accounts Bureau reviewed receipts and disbursements—the upper and lower ranks mutually constrained one another, with nothing lost or omitted.
translations.idiomatic: Under the old system, all revenue and levies throughout the realm were deposited in the Left Storehouse Treasury. The Grand Treasury reported the figures each season, and the Accounts Bureau of the Ministry of Revenue checked receipts and disbursements. Upper and lower offices kept one another in check, and nothing was lost.

sentences.zh: 及第五琦為度支、鹽鐵使，京師多豪將，求取無節，琦不能禁，乃悉以租賦進入大盈內庫，以中人主之意，天子以取給為便，故不復出。

translations.literal: When Diwu Qi became Commissioner of Revenue and the Salt and Iron Monopoly, the capital had many powerful generals who took without restraint. Qi could not forbid this, so he forwarded all land tax and corvée payments into the Daying Inner Treasury to win the eunuchs' favor. The Son of Heaven found direct access convenient, so the funds were never released again.
translations.idiomatic: When Diwu Qi became commissioner of revenue and of the salt and iron monopoly, the capital was full of powerful generals who demanded funds without limit. Qi could not restrain them, so he sent all land tax and corvée payments into the Daying Inner Treasury to please the eunuchs. The emperor found it convenient to draw supplies directly from there, and the funds were never returned to the regular treasury.

sentences.zh: 是以天下公賦，為人君私藏，有司不得窺其多少，國用不能計其贏縮，殆二十年矣。

translations.literal: Thus the public levies of all under Heaven became the private store of the sovereign; officials could not glimpse how much there was, and state expenditures could not be calculated for surplus or deficit—nearly twenty years now.
translations.idiomatic: Public revenue thus became the emperor's private hoard. Officials could not tell how much was on hand, and the state could not calculate surplus or deficit. This had gone on for nearly twenty years.

sentences.zh: 中官以冗名持簿書，領其事者三百人，皆奉給其間，連結根固不可動。

translations.literal: Eunuchs held nominal positions keeping the ledger books; three hundred men managed the affairs, all drawing salaries from it, intertwined and rooted so deeply they could not be moved.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuchs held nominal posts over the account books. Three hundred men ran the operation, all on its payroll, bound together in a network so entrenched that it could not be dislodged.

sentences.zh: 及炎作相，頓首於上前，論之曰：「夫財賦，邦國之大本，生人之喉命，天下理亂輕重皆由焉。

translations.literal: When Yan became chancellor, he prostrated himself before the throne and argued, saying: "Revenue and levies are the great foundation of the state, the throat and life of the people—whether all under Heaven is ordered or chaotic, light or heavy, all depends on them.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Yan became chancellor, he prostrated himself before the throne and argued: "Revenue and taxation are the great foundation of the state and the very life of the people. Whether the realm is well governed or in turmoil, whether it stands firm or falters, all depends on them.

sentences.zh: 是以前代歷選重臣主之，猶懼不集，往往覆敗，大計一失，則天下動搖。

translations.literal: For this reason previous ages repeatedly chose important ministers to oversee them, yet still feared failure—time and again they collapsed. Once the great plan is lost, all under Heaven is shaken.
translations.idiomatic: That is why earlier dynasties repeatedly put great ministers in charge of them, yet still feared failure and often saw the system collapse. Lose control of this great matter, and the whole realm is shaken.

sentences.zh: 先朝權制，中人領其職，以五尺宦豎操邦之本，豐儉盈虛，雖大臣不得知，則無以計天下利害。

translations.literal: The previous reign's improvised measure put eunuchs in charge of the post—a five-foot palace servant holding the foundation of the state; whether there was abundance or scarcity, surplus or deficit, even great ministers could not know, and there was no way to calculate the benefit or harm to all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The previous reign's expedient arrangement put eunuchs in charge—a five-foot palace servant controlling the foundation of the state. Whether funds were plentiful or scarce, in surplus or deficit, even senior ministers could not know, and there was no way to weigh the realm's interests.

sentences.zh: 臣愚待罪宰輔，陛下至德，惟人是恤，參校蠹弊，無斯之甚。

translations.literal: Your foolish servant, bearing the guilt of office as chancellor, finds that Your Majesty's supreme virtue cares for every person; examining and comparing the corruptions, none is worse than this.
translations.idiomatic: Your humble servant, who bears the burden of office as chancellor, sees that Your Majesty's supreme virtue cares for all people. Of the abuses I have examined, none is worse than this.

sentences.zh: 請出之以歸有司，度宮中經費一歲幾何，量數奉入，不敢虧用。

translations.literal: I ask that they be released back to the responsible offices, estimate how much the palace needs for one year's expenses, submit that fixed amount, and not dare waste any.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that these funds be returned to the proper offices, that the palace's annual expenses be estimated, that only the required amount be submitted, and that nothing be squandered.

sentences.zh: 如此，然後可以議政。

translations.literal: Only then may one discuss governing.
translations.idiomatic: Only then can we speak of governing the realm.

sentences.zh: 惟陛下察焉。

translations.literal: I beg Your Majesty to consider this.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to consider it.

sentences.zh: 」詔曰：「凡財賦皆歸左藏庫，一用舊式，每歲於數中量進三五十萬入大盈，而度支先以其全數聞。

translations.literal: " An edict said: "All revenue and levies shall return to the Left Storehouse Treasury, following the old form entirely; each year a fixed amount of three to five hundred thousand shall be forwarded to Daying, while the Department of Revenue first reports the full total."
translations.idiomatic: " An edict replied: "All revenue and levies shall return to the Left Storehouse Treasury according to the old procedure. Each year three to five hundred thousand shall be forwarded to Daying from the total, and the Department of Revenue shall first report the full amount."

sentences.zh: 」炎以片言移人主意，議者以為難，中外稱之。

translations.literal: " With a few words Yan had shifted the sovereign's mind—commentators called it difficult, and court and country praised him.
translations.idiomatic: " With a few words Yang Yan had changed the emperor's mind. Commentators called the feat difficult to achieve, and praise rang through court and country.

sentences.zh: 初定令式，國家有租賦庸調之法。

translations.literal: When statutes and regulations were first set, the state had the system of land tax, labor service, and cloth levy.
translations.idiomatic: When the original statutes were established, the state had the system of land tax, labor service, and cloth levy.

sentences.zh: 開元中，玄宗修道德，以寬仁為理本，故不為版籍之書，人戶浸溢，堤防不禁。

translations.literal: In the Kaiyuan era, Xuanzong cultivated virtue and took leniency and kindness as the basis of rule, so household registers were not kept; population overflowed and dykes could not hold it back.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kaiyuan era, Emperor Xuanzong cultivated virtue and made leniency the basis of rule, so household registers were not maintained. Populations swelled beyond control, and the system could no longer contain them.

sentences.zh: 丁口轉死，非舊名矣；

translations.literal: Able-bodied men died and shifted away—they were no longer on the old rolls;
translations.idiomatic: Able-bodied men died or moved away and were no longer on the old rolls;

sentences.zh: 田畝移換，非舊額矣；

translations.literal: Fields changed hands—they were no longer at the old quotas;
translations.idiomatic: fields changed hands and no longer matched the old quotas;

sentences.zh: 貧富升降，非舊第矣。

translations.literal: Rich and poor rose and fell—they were no longer at the old grades.
translations.idiomatic: the rich and poor rose and fell and no longer fit the old gradations.

sentences.zh: 戶部徒以空文總其故書，蓋得非當時之實。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Revenue merely used empty documents to tally old records—the result was far from current reality.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Revenue could only summarize obsolete records on paper, which bore little relation to actual conditions.

sentences.zh: 舊制，人丁戍邊者，蠲其租庸，六歲免歸。

translations.literal: Under the old system, men drafted for frontier garrison had land tax and corvée remitted; after six years they were exempted and sent home.
translations.idiomatic: Under the old system, men sent to garrison the frontier had their land tax and corvée remitted, and after six years they were released and sent home.

sentences.zh: 玄宗方事夷狄，戍者多死不返，邊將怙寵而諱，不以死申，故其貫籍之名不除。

translations.literal: Xuanzong was then engaged with barbarians; many garrison troops died without returning. Frontier generals, trusting in favor, concealed this and did not report deaths, so their names remained on the household registers.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong was then campaigning against foreign peoples, and many frontier soldiers died without returning. Border generals, secure in imperial favor, concealed the deaths and failed to report them, so the dead remained on the household registers.

sentences.zh: 至天寶中，王鉷為戶口使，方務聚斂，以丁籍且存，則丁身焉往，是隱課而不出耳。

translations.literal: By the Tianbao era, Wang Hong served as Household Registration Commissioner, bent on gathering revenue. Since the rolls still existed, where had the able-bodied men gone?—it was hidden taxation never paid.
translations.idiomatic: By the Tianbao era, Wang Hong served as household registration commissioner and was obsessed with revenue. If the rolls still listed a man, where was his body? The answer was that taxes were being evaded.

sentences.zh: 遂案舊籍，計除六年之外，積征其家三十年租庸。

translations.literal: He then reviewed old registers and, beyond the six-year exemption, collected thirty years of accumulated land tax and corvée from the families.
translations.idiomatic: He then checked the old registers and, beyond the six-year exemption, collected thirty years of accumulated land tax and corvée from the families involved.

sentences.zh: 天下之人苦而無告，則租庸之法弊久矣。

translations.literal: People throughout the realm suffered with no recourse—the land tax and corvée system had been broken for long.
translations.idiomatic: People throughout the realm suffered with no one to whom they could appeal. The land tax and corvée system had been broken for a long time.

sentences.zh: 迨至德之後，天下兵起，始以兵役，因之饑癘，征求運輸，百役並作，人戶雕耗，版圖空虛。

translations.literal: After the Zhide era, armies arose throughout the realm; first came military service, then famine and pestilence; levies and transport demands—all corvées at once. Populations were depleted, territorial registers empty.
translations.idiomatic: After the Zhide era, war spread across the realm. Military service came first, then famine and pestilence; levies, transport, and every kind of corvée fell due at once. Populations were devastated and the registers emptied out.

sentences.zh: 軍國之用，仰給於度支、轉運二使；

translations.literal: Military and state expenses depended on the two commissioners of Revenue and Transport;
translations.idiomatic: Military and state expenses depended on the commissioners of revenue and transport;

sentences.zh: 四方征鎮，又自給於節度、都團練使。

translations.literal: Regional campaigning garrisons likewise supplied themselves through military governors and regional training commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: regional garrisons likewise supplied themselves through military governors and regional training commissioners.

sentences.zh: 賦斂之司數四，而莫相統攝，於是綱目大壞，朝廷不能覆諸使，諸使不能覆諸州，四方貢獻，悉入內庫。

translations.literal: Four tax agencies without mutual oversight—thus the whole system collapsed. The court could not control the commissioners; the commissioners could not control the prefectures. Tribute from all quarters all entered the inner treasury.
translations.idiomatic: There were four revenue agencies with no one to coordinate them, and the whole system fell apart. The court could not oversee the commissioners; the commissioners could not oversee the prefectures. Tribute from every region flowed into the inner treasury.

sentences.zh: 權臣猾吏，因緣為奸，或公托進獻，私為贓盜者動萬萬計。

translations.literal: Powerful ministers and crooked clerks seized the opportunity for villainy—some publicly presenting tribute while privately pilfering sums in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Powerful ministers and corrupt clerks seized the opportunity for fraud. Some used official tribute as a cover while privately embezzling sums in the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 河南、山東、荊襄、劍南有重兵處，皆厚自奉養，王賦所入無幾。

translations.literal: Where heavy troops were stationed—Henan, Shandong, Jingxiang, Jiannan—all richly provisioned themselves; imperial levies yielded little.
translations.idiomatic: In regions where large armies were stationed—Henan, Shandong, Jingxiang, and Jiannan—the commanders lavishly provisioned themselves, and little of the imperial levy reached the center.

sentences.zh: 吏職之名，隨人署置；

translations.literal: Official titles were assigned at will;
translations.idiomatic: Official titles were created at will;

sentences.zh: 俸給厚薄，由其增損。

translations.literal: Salaries thick or thin depended on whoever raised or cut them.
translations.idiomatic: salaries were raised or cut at someone's whim.

sentences.zh: 故科斂之名凡數百，廢者不削，重者不去，新舊仍積，不知其涯。

translations.literal: Thus the names of levies numbered in the hundreds—abolished ones not cut, heavy ones not removed, old and new piled together beyond reckoning.
translations.idiomatic: The names of levies ran into the hundreds. Abolished taxes were not removed, heavy ones were not lightened, and old and new charges piled up beyond reckoning.

sentences.zh: 百姓受命而供之，瀝膏血，鬻親愛，旬輸月送無休息。

translations.literal: The people received orders and supplied them—draining their lifeblood, selling loved ones—delivering every ten days or every month without rest.
translations.idiomatic: The people obeyed orders and paid up, draining their lifeblood and selling their kin, submitting payments every ten days or every month without respite.

sentences.zh: 吏因其苛，蠶食千人。

translations.literal: Officials, exploiting the harshness, gnawed away at the people.
translations.idiomatic: Officials exploited the harsh levies and gnawed away at the people.

sentences.zh: 凡富人多丁者，率為官為僧，以色役免；

translations.literal: Generally rich men with many sons had them become officials or monks to escape labor service;
translations.idiomatic: Wealthy men with many sons usually had them become officials or monks to escape labor service;

sentences.zh: 貧人無所入則丁存。

translations.literal: The poor, having nowhere to register, remained on the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: the poor, with nowhere to hide, remained on the rolls.

sentences.zh: 故課免於上，而賦增於下。

translations.literal: Thus exemptions reached those above while levies increased on those below.
translations.idiomatic: Exemptions went to those above, while the burden on those below grew heavier.

sentences.zh: 是以天下殘瘁，蕩為浮人，鄉居地著者百不四五，如是者殆三十年。

translations.literal: Thus the realm was worn to ruin; people drifted as vagrants—perhaps only four or five in a hundred remained settled in their home villages. This had gone on for nearly thirty years.
translations.idiomatic: The realm was worn to exhaustion. People drifted as vagrants, and perhaps only four or five in a hundred remained settled in their home villages. This had continued for nearly thirty years.

sentences.zh: 炎因奏對，懇言其弊，乃請作兩稅法，以一其名，曰：「凡百役之費，一錢之斂，先度其數而賦於人，量出以制入。

translations.literal: Yan, in a memorial response, spoke earnestly of these abuses and requested creation of the dual-tax system, giving it one name. He said: "All expenses for corvée, every coin of collection—first estimate the total and levy it on the people; measure expenditure to determine income.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yan, in a memorial response, spoke frankly of these abuses and proposed the dual-tax system, giving it a single name. He said: "Every expense for corvée, every coin collected—first estimate the total needed and levy it on the people. Measure expenditure to determine income.

sentences.zh: 戶無主客，以見居為簿；

translations.literal: Households distinguish not native from sojourner—registration follows current residence;
translations.idiomatic: Households shall not be divided into native and sojourner; registration shall follow current residence;

sentences.zh: 人無丁中，以貧富為差。

translations.literal: men distinguish not by male or prime age, but by rich and poor.
translations.idiomatic: and persons shall not be classified by age or sex, but by wealth.

sentences.zh: 不居處而行商者，在所郡縣稅三十之一，度所與居者均，使無僥利。

translations.literal: Those who do not reside locally but trade are taxed one-thirtieth at the prefecture or county where they are, balancing with those who reside locally so none gains unfair advantage.
translations.idiomatic: Merchants who do not reside locally shall pay a tax of one-thirtieth in the prefecture or county where they operate, balanced against local residents so that no one gains an unfair advantage.

sentences.zh: 居人之稅，秋夏兩征之，俗有不便者正之。

translations.literal: Tax on residents is collected twice, in autumn and summer; local customs that prove inconvenient are adjusted.
translations.idiomatic: Tax on residents shall be collected twice, in summer and autumn, with local customs adjusted where they prove inconvenient.

sentences.zh: 其租庸雜徭悉省，而丁額不廢，申報出入如舊式。

translations.literal: Land tax, corvée, and miscellaneous labor services are all abolished, but the quota for able-bodied males is not discarded—reporting arrivals and departures follows the old form.
translations.idiomatic: Land tax, corvée, and miscellaneous labor services shall all be abolished, but the quota for able-bodied males shall remain, with arrivals and departures reported as before.

sentences.zh: 其田畝之稅，率以大歷十四年墾田之數為準而均征之。

translations.literal: Field tax, generally based on the acreage under cultivation in Dali 14, is levied evenly.
translations.idiomatic: Field tax shall generally be assessed evenly on the basis of land under cultivation in Dali 14, 779.

sentences.zh: 夏稅無過六月，秋稅無過十一月。

translations.literal: Summer tax no later than the sixth month; autumn tax no later than the eleventh month.
translations.idiomatic: Summer tax shall be due no later than the sixth month, and autumn tax no later than the eleventh month.

sentences.zh: 逾歲之後，有戶增而稅減輕，及人散而失均者，進退長吏，而以尚書度支總統焉。

translations.literal: After the year passes, if households increase but tax assessments decrease, or if population scatters and equalization fails, superiors and subordinates are promoted or demoted, and the Department of Revenue under the Ministry of Revenue has overall command.
translations.idiomatic: After the year ends, if households increase while tax assessments fall, or if population scatters and equalization fails, local officials shall be promoted or demoted accordingly, and the Department of Revenue shall have overall supervision.

sentences.zh: 」德宗善而行之，詔諭中外。

translations.literal: " Dezong approved and implemented it; an edict announced it to court and country.
translations.idiomatic: " Emperor Dezong approved the plan and put it into effect, and an edict announced it throughout court and country.

sentences.zh: 而掌賦者沮其非利，言租庸之令四百余年，舊制不可輕改。

translations.literal: But those in charge of levies obstructed it as unprofitable, saying the land tax and corvée statute had stood four hundred-odd years—the old system could not lightly be changed.
translations.idiomatic: But officials in charge of taxation objected that it would cut their profits, arguing that the land tax and corvée system had stood for more than four hundred years and that the old order could not lightly be changed.

sentences.zh: 上行之不疑，天下便之。

translations.literal: The emperor carried it out without hesitation; all under Heaven found it convenient.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor carried it out without hesitation, and people throughout the realm found it a relief.

sentences.zh: 人不土斷而地著，賦不加斂而增入，版籍不造而得其虛實，貪吏不誡而奸無所取。

translations.literal: People needed no forced local registration yet settled in place; levies were not increased yet revenue grew; registers were not rebuilt yet truth and falsehood were known; corrupt officials needed no warning yet had no room for villainy.
translations.idiomatic: People settled where they lived without forced registration; revenue increased without raising rates; the true state of the population became known without rebuilding the registers; and corrupt officials found no opening for fraud without even being warned.

sentences.zh: 自是輕重之權，始歸於朝廷。

translations.literal: From this the power to weigh light and heavy returned to the court.
translations.idiomatic: From this point the power to control the fiscal balance returned to the court.

sentences.zh: 炎救時之弊，頗有嘉聲。

translations.literal: Yan remedied the abuses of the age and won considerable praise.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yan remedied the abuses of the age and won considerable praise.

sentences.zh: 蒞事數月，屬崔祐甫疾病，多不視事，喬琳罷免，炎遂獨當國政。

translations.literal: After several months in office, Cui Youfu fell ill and largely ceased handling affairs; Qiao Lin was dismissed—Yan alone bore state governance.
translations.idiomatic: After several months in office, Cui Youfu fell ill and largely stopped attending to affairs. Qiao Lin was dismissed, and Yang Yan alone bore the burden of government.

sentences.zh: 祐甫之所制作，炎隳之。

translations.literal: Whatever Youfu had established, Yan demolished.
translations.idiomatic: Whatever Cui Youfu had established, Yang Yan tore down.

sentences.zh: 初減薄護作元陵功優，人心始不悅。

translations.literal: At first he reduced and cut back the maintenance of construction on the Yuan Mausoleum and bonuses for work—hearts first turned displeased.
translations.idiomatic: At first he cut back maintenance work on the Yuan Mausoleum and reduced bonuses for labor, and public sentiment first turned against him.

sentences.zh: 又專意報恩復仇。

translations.literal: He also devoted himself entirely to repaying kindness and taking revenge.
translations.idiomatic: He also devoted himself single-mindedly to repaying favors and settling scores.

sentences.zh: 道州錄事參軍王沼有微恩於炎，舉沼為監察御史。

translations.literal: Wang Zhao, recorder of Daozhou, had shown Yan a small kindness; Yan recommended Zhao as Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhao, recorder of Daozhou, had once done Yang Yan a small favor, and Yan recommended him as investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 感元載恩，專務行載舊事以報之。

translations.literal: Grateful for Yuan Zai's favor, he devoted himself to carrying out Zai's old policies to repay him.
translations.idiomatic: Grateful for Yuan Zai's past kindness, he devoted himself to carrying out Zai's old policies in repayment.

sentences.zh: 初，載得罪，左僕射劉晏訊劾之，元載誅，炎亦坐貶，故深怨晏。

translations.literal: When Zai fell from grace, Left Vice Director Liu Yan interrogated and impeached him. When Zai was executed, Yan was also implicated and demoted—hence his deep resentment of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Zai fell, Left Vice Director Liu Yan had interrogated and impeached him. When Zai was executed, Yang Yan was implicated and demoted as well, and he bore Liu Yan a deep grudge.

sentences.zh: 晏領東都、河南、江淮、山南東道轉運、租庸、青苗、鹽鐵使，炎作相數月，欲貶晏，先罷其使，天下錢谷皆歸金部、倉部。

translations.literal: Liu Yan held the posts of transport commissioner for the Eastern Capital, Henan, Jiang-Huai, and Shannan East circuits, plus commissioner for corvée, green-sprout, and salt-and-iron levies. Several months after Yan became chancellor, wishing to demote Liu Yan, he first abolished those commissioner posts; all grain and coin revenue under Heaven reverted to the Gold and Granaries bureaus.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yan held the posts of transport commissioner for the Eastern Capital, Henan, Jiang-Huai, and Shannan East circuits, as well as commissioner for corvée, green-sprout, and salt-and-iron levies. Several months after Yang Yan became chancellor, intending to demote Liu Yan, he first abolished those commissioner posts, and all grain and coin revenue throughout the realm reverted to the Gold and Granaries bureaus.

sentences.zh: 又獻議開豐州陵陽渠，發京畿人夫於西城就役，閭裏騷擾，事竟無成。

translations.literal: He also submitted a plan to open the Lingyang Canal at Fengzhou, dispatching corvée laborers from the capital region to work at the western wall—neighborhoods were thrown into turmoil, and in the end nothing was accomplished.
translations.idiomatic: He also proposed opening the Lingyang Canal at Fengzhou and dispatching corvée laborers from the capital region to work on the western wall. Neighborhoods were thrown into turmoil, and in the end nothing was accomplished.

sentences.zh: 初，大歷末，元載議請城原州，以遏西番入寇之沖要，事未行而載誅。

translations.literal: In late Dali, Yuan Zai proposed fortifying Yuan Prefecture to block the vital pass of Western Tibetan incursions—the plan had not been carried out when Zai was executed.
translations.idiomatic: In late Dali, Yuan Zai had proposed fortifying Yuan Prefecture to block the main route of Western Tibetan raids. The plan had not been carried out when Zai was executed.

sentences.zh: 及炎得政，建中二年二月，奏請城原州，先牒涇原節度使段秀實，令為之具。

translations.literal: When Yan gained power, in the second month of Jianzhong 2, he memorialized requesting fortification of Yuan Prefecture, first dispatching a note to Jingyuan Military Governor Duan Xiushi ordering him to make preparations.
translations.idiomatic: Once Yang Yan came to power, in the second month of Jianzhong 2, 781, he memorialized requesting that Yuan Prefecture be fortified and first sent instructions to Duan Xiushi, military governor of Jingyuan, ordering him to make preparations.

sentences.zh: 秀實報曰：「凡安邊卻敵之長策，宜緩以計圖之，無宜草草興功也。

translations.literal: Xiushi replied: "For long-term strategies to secure the border and repel enemies, one should proceed slowly and plan carefully—not hastily launch construction.
translations.idiomatic: Xiushi replied: "The best long-term strategy for securing the border and repelling enemies is to proceed slowly and plan carefully. One should not launch construction in haste.

sentences.zh: 又春事方作，請待農隙而緝其事。

translations.literal: Moreover, spring planting is underway; please wait for the farming interval to undertake this.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, spring planting is underway. Please wait until the farming season ends before undertaking this work.

sentences.zh: 」炎怒，征秀實為司農卿。

translations.literal: " Yan grew angry and summoned Xiushi to be Minister of Agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: " Yang Yan grew angry and recalled Xiushi to serve as minister of agriculture.

sentences.zh: 以邠寧別駕李懷光居前督作，以檢校司空平章事硃泚、御史大夫平章事崔寧各統兵萬人以翼後。

translations.literal: He put Binning Vice Prefect Li Huaiguang in front to supervise construction, with Acting Supervisor of Works and Associate Director Zhu Ci and Censor-in-Chief and Associate Director Cui Ning each commanding ten thousand troops to support from the rear.
translations.idiomatic: He put Li Huaiguang, vice prefect of Binning, in front to supervise construction, while Zhu Ci, acting supervisor of works and associate director, and Cui Ning, censor-in-chief and associate director, each commanded ten thousand troops to support from the rear.

sentences.zh: 三月，詔下涇州為具。

translations.literal: In the third month, an edict was issued to Jingzhou to make preparations.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month an edict was issued ordering Jingzhou to make preparations.

sentences.zh: 涇軍怒而言曰：「吾曹為國西門之屏，十余年矣！

translations.literal: The Jing army angrily declared: "We have been the screen for the state's western gate for more than ten years!
translations.idiomatic: The Jing army erupted in anger, saying: "We have been the shield at the empire's western gate for more than ten years!

sentences.zh: 始治於邠，才置農桑，地著之安；

translations.literal: At first we were stationed at Bin—just as we had established farming and settled down;
translations.idiomatic: At first we were posted to Bin and had just begun to farm and settle down;

sentences.zh: 而徙於此，置榛莽之中，手披足踐，才立城壘；

translations.literal: yet moved here, placed in thicket and bramble, clearing paths by hand and treading with feet, barely establishing ramparts;
translations.idiomatic: then we were transferred here and dumped into the wild brush, hacking paths with our hands and trampling them underfoot just to raise a few ramparts;

sentences.zh: 又投之塞外，吾何罪而置此乎！

translations.literal: moreover cast beyond the frontier—what crime have we committed to be placed here!
translations.idiomatic: now we are thrown beyond the frontier passes. What crime have we committed to deserve this!

sentences.zh: 」李懷光監朔方軍，法令嚴峻，頻殺大將。

translations.literal: " Li Huaiguang supervised the Shuofang army; his laws and orders were severe, and he frequently executed great generals.
translations.idiomatic: " Li Huaiguang supervised the Shuofang army. His laws were harsh, and he frequently executed senior generals.

sentences.zh: 涇州裨將劉文喜因人怨怒，拒不受詔，上疏復求段秀實為帥，否則硃泚。

translations.literal: Jing Prefecture vice general Liu Wenxi, exploiting popular resentment, refused to accept the edict; he memorialized again requesting Duan Xiushi as commander, otherwise Zhu Ci.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Wenxi, a vice general at Jing Prefecture, seized on the soldiers' anger and refused the edict. He memorialized again, demanding Duan Xiushi as commander—or, failing that, Zhu Ci.

sentences.zh: 於是以硃泚代懷光，文喜又不奉詔。

translations.literal: Thereupon Zhu Ci was sent to replace Huaiguang, but Wenxi again refused to obey the edict.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Ci was then sent to replace Huaiguang, but Wenxi again refused to obey.

sentences.zh: 涇有勁兵二萬，閉城拒守，令其子入質吐蕃以求援。

translations.literal: Jing had twenty thousand crack troops; they closed the city and resisted. He sent his son as hostage to the Tibetans to seek aid.
translations.idiomatic: Jing had twenty thousand crack troops. The city was shut and held under siege, and Wenxi sent his son to the Tibetans as a hostage to seek aid.

sentences.zh: 時方炎旱，人情騷動，群臣皆請赦文喜，上皆不省。

translations.literal: At the time there was scorching drought; public sentiment was agitated. All ministers requested pardoning Wenxi—the emperor would not heed any of them.
translations.idiomatic: A scorching drought was then afflicting the region, and public unrest was spreading. Every minister pleaded for Wenxi to be pardoned, but the emperor would hear none of it.

sentences.zh: 德宗減服禦以給軍人，城中軍士當受春服，賜與如故。

translations.literal: Dezong reduced his own rations to supply the troops. Soldiers in the city who were due spring uniforms were granted them as before.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Dezong cut his own provisions to feed the besieging troops. The soldiers inside the city, due their spring uniforms, received them as usual.

sentences.zh: 命硃泚、李懷光等軍攻之，乃築壘環之。

translations.literal: He ordered Zhu Ci, Li Huaiguang, and other armies to attack; they then built ramparts to encircle the city.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Zhu Ci, Li Huaiguang, and other forces to attack, and they built encircling ramparts around the city.

sentences.zh: 涇州別將劉海賓斬文喜首，傳之闕下。

translations.literal: Jing Prefecture vice commander Liu Haibin beheaded Wenxi and sent the head to the palace gate.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Haibin, a vice commander at Jing Prefecture, beheaded Wenxi and sent his head to the palace.

sentences.zh: 茍非海賓效順，必生邊患，皆因炎以喜怒易帥，涇帥結怨故也。

translations.literal: Had Haibin not submitted, border calamity would surely have arisen—all because Yan changed commanders on whim, causing the Jing commander to harbor enmity.
translations.idiomatic: Had Haibin not turned loyal, a border disaster would surely have followed—all because Yang Yan had replaced commanders on whim and bred resentment among the Jing garrison.

sentences.zh: 原州竟不能城。

translations.literal: Yuan Prefecture in the end could not be fortified.
translations.idiomatic: In the end Yuan Prefecture was never fortified.

sentences.zh: 炎既構劉晏之罪貶官，司農卿庾淮與晏有隙，乃用準為荊南節度使，諷令誣晏以忠州叛，殺之，妻子徙嶺表，朝野為之側目。

translations.literal: After Yan had fabricated charges against Liu Yan and demoted him, Minister of Agriculture Yu Huai, who had a rift with Liu Yan, was then appointed Jingnan military governor; he was instructed to frame Liu Yan for rebellion at Zhong Prefecture, have him killed, and his wife and children were exiled beyond the mountain passes; court and countryside looked askance.
translations.idiomatic: After Yang Yan had trumped up charges against Liu Yan and had him demoted, Yu Huai, minister of agriculture, who bore a grudge against Liu Yan, was appointed military governor of Jingnan and instructed to accuse Liu Yan of rebellion at Zhong Prefecture and have him killed. Liu Yan's wife and children were exiled beyond the Lingnan passes, and all of court and countryside looked on in dismay.

sentences.zh: 李正己上表請殺晏之罪，指斥朝廷。

translations.literal: Li Zhengji submitted a memorial regarding the crime of killing Liu Yan, censuring the court.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhengji submitted a memorial protesting Liu Yan's murder and denouncing the court.

sentences.zh: 炎懼，乃遣腹心分往諸道：裴冀，東都、河陽、魏博；

translations.literal: Yan grew afraid and dispatched trusted confidants to the various circuits in turn: Pei Ji—to the Eastern Capital, Heyang, and Weibo;
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yan grew afraid and sent trusted agents to the various circuits: Pei Ji to the Eastern Capital, Heyang, and Weibo;

sentences.zh: 孫成，澤潞、磁邢、幽州；

translations.literal: Sun Cheng—to Zelu, Cixing, and You Prefecture;
translations.idiomatic: Sun Cheng to Zelu, Cixing, and You Prefecture;

sentences.zh: 盧東美，河南、淄青；

translations.literal: Lu Dongmei—to Henan and Ziqing;
translations.idiomatic: Lu Dongmei to Henan and Ziqing;

sentences.zh: 李舟，山南、湖南；

translations.literal: Li Zhou—to Shannan and Hunan;
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhou to Shannan and Hunan;

sentences.zh: 王定，淮西。

translations.literal: Wang Ding—to Huaixi.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ding to Huaixi.

sentences.zh: 聲言宣慰，而意實說謗。

translations.literal: They claimed to go as consolation envoys, but in fact intended to slander.
translations.idiomatic: They claimed to be going as consolation envoys, but in fact meant to spread slander.

sentences.zh: 且言「晏之得罪，以昔年附會奸邪，謀立獨孤妃為皇后，上自惡之，非他過也。

translations.literal: And they said: "Liu Yan's offense was that in former years he joined with wicked men to plot making Consort Dugu queen—the emperor himself detested this; there was no other fault."
translations.idiomatic: They also said, "Liu Yan's offense was that years ago he joined with wicked men to plot making Consort Dugu empress. The emperor himself loathed this; there was no other crime."

sentences.zh: 」或有密奏「炎遣五使往諸鎮者，恐天下以殺劉晏之罪歸己，推過於上耳。

translations.literal: " Some submitted secret memorials: "Yan dispatching five envoys to the various garrisons—he fears the empire will ascribe Liu Yan's murder to himself and is shifting blame onto the emperor."
translations.idiomatic: " Someone submitted a secret memorial: "Yang Yan is sending five envoys to the military circuits because he fears the realm will hold him responsible for Liu Yan's murder and is shifting the blame onto Your Majesty."

sentences.zh: 」乃使中人復炎辭於正己，還報信然。

translations.literal: " The emperor then sent a eunuch to relay Yan's words to Zhengji; on return he reported they were indeed so.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor then sent a eunuch to repeat Yang Yan's words to Li Zhengji; on his return the eunuch reported that Zhengji had indeed heard them.

sentences.zh: 自此德宗有意誅炎矣，待事而發。

translations.literal: From this Dezong intended to execute Yan, waiting for an occasion to act.
translations.idiomatic: From this point Emperor Dezong resolved to destroy Yang Yan and waited for an opportunity to strike.

sentences.zh: 乃擢用盧杞為門下侍郎、平章事，炎轉中書侍郎，仍平章事。

translations.literal: He then promoted Lu Qi to Vice Director of the Chancellery and Associate Director; Yan was transferred to Vice Director of the Secretariat, still Associate Director.
translations.idiomatic: He then promoted Lu Qi to vice director of the Chancellery and associate director, while Yang Yan was transferred to vice director of the Secretariat, retaining his associate directorship.

sentences.zh: 二人同事秉政，杞無文學，儀貌寢陋，炎惡而忽之，每托疾息於他閣，多不會食，杞亦銜恨之。

translations.literal: The two served together wielding government. Qi had no literary cultivation; his bearing and appearance were unsightly. Yan despised and disregarded him, often pleading illness to rest in another pavilion and frequently not dining together; Qi also nursed resentment.
translations.idiomatic: The two served together as chief ministers. Lu Qi had no literary training and an unprepossessing appearance. Yang Yan despised and ignored him, often pleading illness to rest in another pavilion and frequently skipping joint meals. Lu Qi nursed his resentment in turn.

sentences.zh: 舊制，中書舍人分押尚書六曹，以平奏報，開元初廢其職，杞請復之，炎固以為不可。

translations.literal: By old regulation, Secretariat drafters divided supervision of the Six Boards of the Department of State Affairs to balance memorial reports. In early Kaiyuan this office was abolished. Qi requested its restoration; Yan firmly held it impossible.
translations.idiomatic: Under the old system, secretariat drafters had divided supervision of the six boards of the Department of State Affairs to review memorials and reports. Early in the Kaiyuan era that function was abolished. Lu Qi asked to restore it; Yang Yan firmly opposed the idea.

sentences.zh: 杞益怒，又密啟中書主書過，逐之。

translations.literal: Qi grew angrier still; he also secretly reported offenses of the chief secretary of the Secretariat and had him driven out.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Qi grew still angrier and secretly reported misconduct by the secretariat's chief clerk, having him expelled.

sentences.zh: 炎怒曰：「主書，吾局吏也，有過吾自治之，奈何而相侵？」

translations.literal: Yan angrily said: "The chief secretary is an officer under my jurisdiction—if he has fault I will discipline him myself. How dare you encroach?"
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yan said in anger, "The chief clerk is an officer under my office. If he has done wrong I will punish him myself. How dare you interfere?"

sentences.zh: 屬梁崇義叛換，德宗欲以淮西節度使李希烈統諸軍討之。

translations.literal: At the time Liang Chongyi rebelled and switched allegiance. Dezong wished to have Huaixi Military Governor Li Xilie command the various armies to suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Liang Chongyi rebelled and changed sides. Emperor Dezong wanted Li Xilie, military governor of Huaixi, to command the various armies against him.

sentences.zh: 炎諫曰：「希烈始與李忠臣為子，親任無雙，竟逐忠臣而取其位，背本若此，豈可信也！

translations.literal: Yan remonstrated: "Xilie at first treated Li Zhongchen as a father, enjoying unmatched intimate trust, yet in the end drove Zhongchen out and seized his position. To betray one's roots like this—how can he be trusted!"
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yan remonstrated, "Xilie at first treated Li Zhongchen as a father and enjoyed unmatched trust, yet in the end drove Zhongchen out and seized his post. A man who betrays his roots like this—how can he be trusted!"

sentences.zh: 居常無尺寸功，猶強不奉法，異日平賊後，恃功邀上，陛下何以馭之？

translations.literal: In ordinary times he has not an inch of merit, yet still forcibly defies the law. If someday after pacifying the rebels he relies on merit to demand rewards from Your Majesty—how will Your Majesty control him?"
translations.idiomatic: In ordinary times he has not a shred of merit, yet still defies the law with impunity. If one day, after the rebels are crushed, he uses his service to make demands on Your Majesty, how will Your Majesty restrain him?"

sentences.zh: 」初，炎之南來，途經襄、漢，固勸崇義入朝，崇義不能從，已懷反側。

translations.literal: " Earlier, when Yan came south, passing through Xiang and Han, he strongly urged Chongyi to enter court; Chongyi could not comply and already harbored disloyal intent.
translations.idiomatic: " Earlier, when Yang Yan came south and passed through Xiang and Han, he had strongly urged Chongyi to come to court. Chongyi could not comply and already harbored rebellious intent.

sentences.zh: 尋又使其黨李舟使馳說，崇義固而拒命，遂圖叛逆，皆炎迫而成之。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Yan also had his clique-member Li Zhou rush to persuade; Chongyi stubbornly refused orders and then plotted rebellion—all forced into being by Yan's pressure.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Yang Yan also sent his ally Li Zhou to hurry and persuade him. Chongyi stubbornly refused his orders and then plotted rebellion—all of it brought on by Yang Yan's pressure.

sentences.zh: 至是，德宗欲假希烈兵勢以討崇義，然後別圖希烈。

translations.literal: At this point Dezong wished to borrow Xilie's military strength to attack Chongyi, then separately deal with Xilie.
translations.idiomatic: At this point Emperor Dezong meant to borrow Xilie's military strength to crush Chongyi, then deal with Xilie separately.

sentences.zh: 炎又固言不可，上不能平，乃曰：「朕業許之矣，不能食言。

translations.literal: Yan again firmly said it could not be done. The emperor could not remain calm and said: "I have already promised—I cannot break my word."
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yan again insisted it could not be done. The emperor, unable to contain his irritation, said, "I have already given my word. I cannot go back on it."

sentences.zh: 」遂以希烈統諸軍。

translations.literal: " Xilie was thereupon put in command of the various armies.
translations.idiomatic: " Li Xilie was thereupon put in overall command of the armies.

sentences.zh: 會德宗嘗訪宰相群臣中可以大任者，盧杞薦張鎰、嚴郢，而炎舉崔昭、趙惠伯。

translations.literal: Once when Dezong asked the chancellors and ministers whom among the officials could be entrusted with great responsibility, Lu Qi recommended Zhang Yi and Yan Ying, while Yan recommended Cui Zhao and Zhao Huibo.
translations.idiomatic: On one occasion Emperor Dezong asked the chief ministers which officials could be entrusted with great responsibility. Lu Qi recommended Zhang Yi and Yan Ying, while Yang Yan recommended Cui Zhao and Zhao Huibo.

sentences.zh: 上以炎論議疏闊，遂罷炎相，為左僕射。

translations.literal: The emperor considered Yan's policy discussions shallow and broad-minded, and therefore removed him from the chancellorship, making him Left Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor judged Yang Yan's policy counsel shallow and unfocused and therefore removed him from the chancellorship, appointing him left vice director instead.

sentences.zh: 後數日中謝，對於延英，及出，馳歸，不至中書，盧杞自是益怒焉。

translations.literal: Several days later at the mid-day audience of thanks in Yanying Hall—when he came out he galloped home and did not go to the Secretariat; from this Lu Qi grew angrier still.
translations.idiomatic: Several days later, at the midday audience of thanks in Yanying Hall, Yang Yan galloped straight home when it ended and did not go to the Secretariat. From this Lu Qi grew angrier still.

sentences.zh: 杞尋引嚴郢為御史大夫。

translations.literal: Qi soon brought in Yan Ying as Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Qi soon brought in Yan Ying as censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 初，郢為京兆尹，不附炎，炎怒之，諷御史張著彈郢，郢罷兼御史中丞。

translations.literal: At first, when Ying was Metropolitan Governor of Jingzhao, he did not attach himself to Yan; Yan grew angry and prompted Censor Zhang Zhuo to impeach Ying; Ying was dismissed from his additional post as Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Yan Ying was metropolitan governor of Jingzhao, he had refused to attach himself to Yang Yan. Yang Yan grew angry and prompted Censor Zhang Zhuo to impeach him, and Yan Ying was stripped of his additional post as vice censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 炎又夙聞源休與郢有隙，乃拔休自流人為京兆尹，令伺郢過。

translations.literal: Yan had long heard that Yuan Xiu and Ying had a rift; he therefore pulled Xiu from exile to make him Metropolitan Governor, ordering him to watch for Ying's faults.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yan had long known that Yuan Xiu and Yan Ying were at odds. He therefore pulled Xiu from exile and made him metropolitan governor, ordering him to watch for Yan Ying's faults.

sentences.zh: 休蒞官後，與郢友善，炎大怒。

translations.literal: After Xiu took office he became friendly with Ying; Yan was greatly enraged.
translations.idiomatic: After Yuan Xiu took office he became friendly with Yan Ying, and Yang Yan was furious.

sentences.zh: 張光晟方謀議殺回紇酋帥，炎乃以休為入回紇使，休幾為虜所殺。

translations.literal: Zhang Guangcheng was just plotting to kill the Uyghur chieftain; Yan therefore sent Xiu as envoy to the Uyghurs, and Xiu nearly was killed by the barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Guangcheng was then plotting to kill the Uyghur chieftain, so Yang Yan sent Yuan Xiu as envoy to the Uyghurs. Xiu nearly lost his life among them.

sentences.zh: 郢尋坐以度田不實，改為大理卿，時人惜之。

translations.literal: Ying soon was convicted on grounds of inaccurate land surveys and was changed to Chief of the Court of Judicial Review; people of the time regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Ying was soon convicted on a charge of falsifying land surveys and was transferred to chief of the Court of Judicial Review. People of the time regretted the loss.

sentences.zh: 至是，杞因群情所欲，又知郢與炎有隙，故引薦之。

translations.literal: At this point Qi, following what public sentiment desired and knowing Ying's rift with Yan, therefore recommended him.
translations.idiomatic: At this point Lu Qi, following what public opinion wanted and knowing Yan Ying's rift with Yang Yan, therefore recommended him.

sentences.zh: 炎子弘業不肖，多犯禁，受賂請托，郢按之，兼得其他過。

translations.literal: Yan's son Hongye was worthless, frequently violating prohibitions and accepting bribes for petitions; Ying investigated him and also uncovered other offenses.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yan's son Hongye was worthless, repeatedly breaking the law and taking bribes for favors. Yan Ying investigated him and uncovered other offenses as well.

sentences.zh: 初，炎將立家廟，先有私第在東都，令河南尹趙惠伯貨之，惠伯為炎市為官廨。

translations.literal: At first, when Yan was about to establish a family temple, he already had a private residence in the Eastern Capital; he ordered Henan Governor Zhao Huibo to purchase it—Huibo bought it for Yan as an official office building.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Yang Yan was about to establish a family temple, he already owned a private residence in the Eastern Capital. He ordered Zhao Huibo, governor of Henan, to buy it for him, and Huibo purchased it on Yang Yan's behalf as an official office building.

sentences.zh: 時惠伯自河中尹、都團練觀察等使初受代，郢奏追捕惠伯詰案。

translations.literal: At the time Huibo had just been replaced as Governor of Hezhong and overall defense-and-observation commissioner; Ying memorialized to pursue and arrest Huibo for interrogation.
translations.idiomatic: Huibo had just been replaced as governor of Hezhong and overall defense-and-observation commissioner. Yan Ying memorialized to pursue and arrest him for interrogation.

sentences.zh: 御史以炎為宰相，抑吏貨市私第，貴估其宅，賤入其幣，計以為贓。

translations.literal: The censors held that Yan as chancellor had coerced an official to purchase his private residence, overvaluing the house and underpaying the price—calculated as embezzlement.
translations.idiomatic: The censors held that Yang Yan, as chancellor, had coerced an official into buying his private residence, overvaluing the property and underpaying the price—a sum calculated as embezzlement.

sentences.zh: 杞召大理正田晉評罪，晉曰：「宰臣於庶官，比之監臨，官市賈有羨利，計其利以乞取論罪，當奪官。

translations.literal: Qi summoned Chief Judge of the Court of Judicial Review Tian Jin to assess the crime. Jin said: "A chancellor toward ordinary officials is comparable to a supervisor—if an official purchase yields surplus profit, calculating that profit as solicited bribe, the penalty should be removal from office."
translations.idiomatic: Lu Qi summoned Tian Jin, chief judge of the Court of Judicial Review, to assess the crime. Jin said, "A chancellor toward ordinary officials is like a supervisor over subordinates. If an official purchase yields surplus profit, and that profit is calculated as a solicited bribe, the penalty should be removal from office."

sentences.zh: 」杞怒，謫晉衡州司馬。

translations.literal: " Qi was angry and demoted Jin to staff administrator of Heng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: " Lu Qi was furious and demoted Jin to staff administrator of Heng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 更召他吏繩之，曰：「監主自盜，罪絞。

translations.literal: He summoned another official to apply the statute, who said: "Supervisor stealing from himself—punishment strangulation."
translations.idiomatic: He summoned another official to apply the statute, who said, "A supervisor who steals from himself—punishment by strangulation."

sentences.zh: 」開元中，蕭嵩將於曲江南立私廟，尋以玄宗臨幸之所，恐置廟非便，乃罷之。

translations.literal: In Kaiyuan, Xiao Song was about to establish a private temple south of Qu River; soon because it was a place Emperor Xuanzong visited, fearing a temple there would be inappropriate, he abandoned the plan.
translations.idiomatic: In the Kaiyuan era, Xiao Song was about to establish a private temple south of Qu River, but because it was a place Emperor Xuanzong frequented, he feared a temple there would be inappropriate and abandoned the plan.

sentences.zh: 至是，炎以其地為廟，有飛語者云：「此地有王氣，炎故取之，必有異圖。

translations.literal: At this point Yan made that site his temple. Someone spread rumors: "This place has royal qi; Yan took it for that reason—he must harbor treasonous designs."
translations.idiomatic: Now Yang Yan made that very site his temple. Rumors spread: "This place has royal qi. Yang Yan took it for that reason—he must harbor treasonous designs."

sentences.zh: 」語聞，上愈怒。

translations.literal: " When the words were heard, the emperor grew angrier still.
translations.idiomatic: " When word reached the emperor, his anger grew still fiercer.

sentences.zh: 及臺司上具獄，詔三司使同覆之。

translations.literal: When the censorate submitted the complete case, an edict ordered the Three Offices commissioners to review it jointly.
translations.idiomatic: When the censorate submitted the full case, an edict ordered the commissioners of the Three Offices to review it jointly.

sentences.zh: 建中二年十月，詔曰：「尚書左僕射楊炎，托以文藝，累登清貫。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of Jianzhong 2, an edict said: "Left Vice Director of the Department Yang Yan, relying on literary accomplishments, repeatedly ascended to eminent posts.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of Jianzhong 2, 781, an edict declared, "Left Vice Director Yang Yan, relying on literary talent, rose repeatedly to eminent posts.

sentences.zh: 雖謫居荒服，而虛稱猶存。

translations.literal: Although banished to barbarian regions, empty reputation still remained.
translations.idiomatic: Though once banished to the frontier, his empty reputation still lingered.

sentences.zh: 朕初臨萬邦，思弘大化，務擢非次，招納時髦。

translations.literal: When I first assumed rule over the myriad states, I wished to extend great transformation, striving to promote beyond the usual order and recruit men of the age.
translations.idiomatic: When I first took the throne, I wished to extend great reform, striving to promote men out of turn and recruit the finest talent of the age.

sentences.zh: 拔自郡佐，登於鼎司，獨委心膂，信任無疑。

translations.literal: Raised from a prefectural aide to the highest ministry, I entrusted him alone as heart and backbone, trusting without doubt.
translations.idiomatic: Raised from a prefectural aide to the highest ministry, I entrusted him alone as my right hand, trusting him without reservation.

sentences.zh: 而乃不思竭誠，敢為奸蠹，進邪醜正，既偽且堅，黨援因依，動涉情故。

translations.literal: Yet he did not think to exhaust loyalty, dared to be a wicked scourge, advancing the wicked and disgracing the upright—both false and stubborn, factional support and mutual dependence, every move touching on personal ties.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he did not think to serve with full loyalty. He dared to be a wicked scourge, advancing the corrupt and disgracing the upright—false and stubborn alike, building factions and clinging to patrons, every move tangled in private ties.

sentences.zh: 隳法敗度，罔上行私，茍利其身，不顧於國。

translations.literal: He destroyed law and violated measure, deceived the ruler and pursued private ends, seeking only his own profit without regard for the state.
translations.idiomatic: He destroyed law and violated proper measure, deceived his ruler and pursued private ends, seeking only his own profit with no regard for the state.

sentences.zh: 加以內無訓誡，外有交通，縱恣詐欺，以成贓賄。

translations.literal: Moreover internally without instruction and restraint, externally maintaining illicit connections, indulging fraud and deceit to achieve embezzlement and bribes.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, he lacked restraint at home and kept illicit contacts abroad, indulging fraud and deceit until embezzlement and bribery followed.

sentences.zh: 詢其事跡，本末乖謬，蔑恩棄德，負我何深！

translations.literal: Inquiring into his deeds from start to finish—contradictory and erroneous; scorning kindness and abandoning virtue—how deeply he has failed me!
translations.idiomatic: Inquiring into his deeds from beginning to end, the record is contradictory and false. Scorning kindness and abandoning virtue—how deeply he has betrayed me!

sentences.zh: 考狀議刑，罪在難宥。

translations.literal: Examining the facts and deliberating punishment—his crime is hard to pardon.
translations.idiomatic: Examining the facts and deliberating punishment, his crime admits no pardon.

sentences.zh: 但以朕於將相，義切始終，顧全大體，特有弘貸，俾從遠謫，以肅具僚。

translations.literal: But because I toward generals and ministers observe the bond from beginning to end, looking to the larger framework, I specially grant leniency, allowing distant banishment to admonish all officials.
translations.idiomatic: But because I hold generals and ministers to the bond from beginning to end and look to the larger good, I grant special leniency and allow distant banishment, that all officials may take warning.

sentences.zh: 可崖州司馬同正，仍馳驛發遣。

translations.literal: He may be appointed Acting Assistant Administrator of Yazhou, still dispatched by fast courier relay.
translations.idiomatic: He is appointed acting assistant administrator of Yazhou and dispatched by fast relay.

sentences.zh: 」去崖州百里賜死，年五十五。

translations.literal: " One hundred li from Yazhou he was granted death. He was fifty-five years old.
translations.idiomatic: " One hundred li from Yazhou he was granted death. He was fifty-five years old.

sentences.zh: 炎早有文章，亦勵誌節，及為中書舍人，附會元載，時議已薄之。

translations.literal: Yan early had literary talent and also cultivated moral resolve; when he became Secretariat drafter he attached himself to Yuan Zai—public opinion already held him in low esteem.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yan had shown literary talent early and cultivated moral resolve, but when he became a secretariat drafter he attached himself to Yuan Zai, and public opinion already held him in low esteem.

sentences.zh: 後坐載貶官，憤恚益甚，歸而得政，睚眥必仇，險害之性附於心，唯其愛憎，不顧公道，以至於敗。

translations.literal: Later implicated with Zai he was demoted; resentment grew fiercer. Returning and gaining power, he avenged every grudge; treacherous and harmful nature attached to his heart—following only his loves and hates without regard for public justice, until ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Later implicated with Zai, he was demoted and his resentment grew fiercer. Returning to power, he avenged every slight. A treacherous and harmful nature took hold of him; he followed only his loves and hates without regard for justice, until ruin came.

sentences.zh: 惠伯亦坐炎貶費州多田尉，尋亦殺之。

translations.literal: Huibo was also implicated with Yan and demoted to assistant magistrate of Duotian in Feizhou; soon he too was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Huibo was also implicated with Yang Yan and demoted to assistant magistrate of Duotian in Feizhou; soon he too was executed.

sentences.zh: 黎幹者，戎州人。

translations.literal: Li Gan was a native of Rong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Li Gan was a native of Rong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 始以善星緯數術進，待詔翰林，累官至諫議大夫。

translations.literal: At first he advanced through skill in astronomy, the calendar, and numerical arts; he served as Hanlin draft attendant and rose through posts to Remonstrance Adviser.
translations.idiomatic: At first he advanced through skill in astronomy, calendrics, and numerology. He served as a Hanlin draft attendant and rose through the ranks to remonstrance adviser.

sentences.zh: 尋遷京兆尹，以嚴肅為理，人頗便之，而因緣附會，與時上下。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Metropolitan Governor of Jingzhao; he governed with severity and the people found it convenient, yet he opportunistically attached himself to power and rose and fell with the times.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was transferred to metropolitan governor of Jingzhao. He governed with severity and the people found it helpful, yet he opportunistically attached himself to power and rose and fell with the times.

sentences.zh: 大歷二年，改刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: In Dali 2 he was changed to Vice Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: In Dali 2, 767, he was transferred to vice minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 魚朝恩伏誅，坐交通出為桂州刺史、本管觀察使。

translations.literal: When Yu Chao'en was executed he was implicated for illicit contact and sent out as Prefect of Guizhou and observer of that circuit.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu Chao'en was executed, Li Gan was implicated for illicit contact and sent out as prefect of Guizhou and observer of that circuit.

sentences.zh: 至江陵，丁母憂。

translations.literal: Reaching Jiangling he entered mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: Reaching Jiangling, he entered mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 久之，會京兆尹缺，人頗思幹。

translations.literal: After a long while, when the post of Metropolitan Governor was vacant, people greatly missed Gan.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval, when the post of metropolitan governor fell vacant, people greatly missed Li Gan.

sentences.zh: 八年，復拜京兆尹、兼御史大夫。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was again appointed Metropolitan Governor, concurrently Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In Dali 8, 773, he was again appointed metropolitan governor, concurrently censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 幹自以得誌，無心為理，貪暴益甚，徇於財色。

translations.literal: Gan, thinking he had achieved his ambition, had no heart for governance; greed and brutality grew worse; he indulged wealth and women.
translations.idiomatic: Li Gan, thinking he had achieved his ambition, had no heart for governing. Greed and brutality grew worse, and he indulged himself in wealth and women.

sentences.zh: 十三年，除兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he was removed and made Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: In Dali 13, 778, he was removed and appointed vice minister of war.

sentences.zh: 性險，挾左道，結中貴，以希主恩，代宗甚惑之。

translations.literal: His nature was treacherous; he relied on heterodox arts, cultivated connections with inner favorites to seek imperial favor—Emperor Daizong was greatly influenced by him.
translations.idiomatic: His nature was treacherous. He relied on heterodox arts and cultivated connections with palace favorites to seek imperial favor, and Emperor Daizong was greatly influenced by him.

sentences.zh: 時中官劉忠翼寵任方盛，幹結之素厚，嘗通其奸謀。

translations.literal: At the time the inner attendant Liu Zhongyi's favor and trust were at their height; Gan had long been bound to him and once communicated with him in treacherous plots.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the palace attendant Liu Zhongyi enjoyed peak favor and trust. Li Gan had long been bound to him and once shared treacherous plots with him.

sentences.zh: 及德宗初即位，幹猶以詭道求進，密居輿中詣忠翼第。

translations.literal: When Dezong first ascended the throne, Gan still sought advancement through deceptive arts, traveling secretly in a closed carriage to Liu Zhongyi's residence.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Dezong first ascended the throne, Li Gan still sought advancement through deceptive arts, traveling secretly in a closed carriage to Liu Zhongyi's residence.

sentences.zh: 事發，詔曰：「兵部侍郎黎幹，害若豺狼，特進劉忠翼，掩義隱賊，並除名長流。

translations.literal: When the affair broke, an edict said: "Vice Minister of War Li Gan—harmful as a wolf; Special Advancement Liu Zhongyi—concealing righteousness and harboring villains—both stripped of names and exiled far."
translations.idiomatic: When the affair broke, an edict declared, "Vice Minister of War Li Gan is harmful as a wolf; Special Advancement Liu Zhongyi conceals righteousness and harbors villains. Both are stripped of rank and exiled far."

sentences.zh: 」即行，市裏兒童數千人噪聚，懷瓦礫投擊之，捕賊尉不能止，遂皆賜死於藍田驛。

translations.literal: " As they were sent off, several thousand children of the marketplace gathered in uproar, carrying tiles and stones to pelt them; the constable for catching robbers could not stop them. They were then both granted death at Lantian Post.
translations.idiomatic: " As they were sent off, several thousand marketplace children gathered in uproar, carrying tiles and stones to pelt them. The constable charged with catching robbers could not stop the mob. Both were then granted death at Lantian Post.

sentences.zh: 忠翼，宦官也，本名清潭，與董秀皆有寵於代宗。

translations.literal: Zhongyi was a eunuch; his original name was Qingtan. He and Dong Xiu both enjoyed favor with Daizong.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhongyi was a eunuch; his original name was Qingtan. He and Dong Xiu both enjoyed favor with Emperor Daizong.

sentences.zh: 天憲在口，勢回日月，貪饕納賄，貨產巨萬。

translations.literal: Imperial authority rested on his lips; his power bent sun and moon; insatiably greedy, accepting bribes—property in the tens of millions.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial authority rested on his lips; his power seemed to turn sun and moon. Insatiably greedy and taking bribes, he amassed property worth tens of millions.

sentences.zh: 大歷中，德宗居東宮，幹及清潭嘗有奸謀動搖。

translations.literal: In Dali, when Dezong resided in the Eastern Palace, Gan and Qingtan once had treacherous plots to shake the succession.
translations.idiomatic: During the Dali era, while Emperor Dezong was crown prince in the Eastern Palace, Li Gan and Qingtan once plotted treacherously to shake the succession.

sentences.zh: 及是，積前罪以誅之。

translations.literal: At this time accumulated previous crimes were the grounds for executing them.
translations.idiomatic: On this occasion accumulated earlier crimes became the grounds for their execution.

sentences.zh: 庾準，常州人。

translations.literal: Yu Zhun was a native of Chang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Zhun was a native of Chang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父光先，天寶中，文部侍郎。

translations.literal: His father Guangxian was Vice Minister of Culture during Tianbao.
translations.idiomatic: His father Guangxian had been vice minister of the Ministry of Rites during the Tianbao era.

sentences.zh: 準以門入仕，昵於宰相王縉，縉驟引至職方郎中、知制誥，遷中書舍人。

translations.literal: Zhun entered office through family connections; intimate with Chancellor Wang Jin, Jin swiftly promoted him to Director of Appointments in the Ministry of War, with control of edict drafts, then to Secretariat drafter.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Zhun entered office through family connections. Close to Chancellor Wang Jin, Jin swiftly promoted him to director of appointments in the Ministry of War with control of edict drafts, then to secretariat drafter.

sentences.zh: 準素寡文學，以柔媚自進，既非儒流，甚為時論所薄。

translations.literal: Zhun was always lacking in literary cultivation, advancing through flattery; not being of the Confucian stream, he was much slighted in contemporary opinion.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Zhun had little literary training and advanced through flattery. Not being of the Confucian scholarly stream, he was widely slighted in contemporary opinion.

sentences.zh: 尋改御史中丞，遷尚書左丞。

translations.literal: Soon he was changed to Vice Censor-in-Chief, then promoted to Left Assistant Director of the Department.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was transferred to vice censor-in-chief, then promoted to left assistant director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 縉得罪，出為汝州刺史。

translations.literal: When Jin was implicated he was sent out as Prefect of Ru Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Jin fell from power, Yu Zhun was sent out as prefect of Ru Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 復入為司農卿，與楊炎厚善。

translations.literal: He returned again as Minister of Agriculture, thick friends with Yang Yan.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to court as minister of agriculture and became close friends with Yang Yan.

sentences.zh: 炎欲殺劉晏，知準與晏有隙，乃用為荊南節度。

translations.literal: Yan wished to kill Liu Yan; knowing Zhun had a rift with Yan, he appointed him Jingnan military governor.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yan wished to kill Liu Yan. Knowing Yu Zhun bore a grudge against Liu Yan, he appointed him military governor of Jingnan.

sentences.zh: 準乃上言得晏與硃泚書，且有怨望，又召補州兵以拒命。

translations.literal: Zhun thereupon memorialized upward that he had obtained letters between Yan and Zhu Ci, and moreover that Yan harbored resentment, and had also summoned and supplemented prefectural troops to resist orders.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Zhun then memorialized that he had obtained correspondence between Liu Yan and Zhu Ci, that Yan harbored resentment against the throne, and that he had raised supplemental troops in defiance of orders.

sentences.zh: 於是先殺晏，然後下詔賜自盡，海內冤之。

translations.literal: Thereupon they first killed Yan, then issued an edict granting suicide; all within the seas considered it unjust.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yan was killed first; only afterward was an edict issued ordering him to take his own life. The empire regarded it as a gross injustice.

sentences.zh: 炎以殺晏征準為尚書左丞。

translations.literal: Yan, for killing Yan, summoned Zhun back as Left Vice Director of the Ministry of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yan recalled Yu Zhun to court as left vice director of the Ministry of State Affairs as reward for killing Liu Yan.

sentences.zh: 建中三年六月丁巳卒，時年五十一。

translations.literal: On dingsi, the sixth month of the third year of Jianzhong, he died, aged fifty-one.
translations.idiomatic: He died on dingsi day in the sixth month of Jianzhong 3, 782, at the age of fifty-one.

sentences.zh: 贈工部尚書。

translations.literal: He was posthumously given Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously appointed minister of works.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：仲尼云：富與貴是人之欲，不以道得之不處。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: Confucius said: Wealth and honor are what people desire; if one does not obtain them by the Way, one does not dwell in them.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer writes: Confucius said that wealth and honor are what people desire, but that one must not accept them unless gained by the Way.

sentences.zh: 反乎是道者小人。

translations.literal: Those who oppose this Way are petty men.
translations.idiomatic: Those who act contrary to this principle are petty men.

sentences.zh: 載諂輔國以進身，弄時權而固位，眾怒難犯，長惡不悛，家亡而誅及妻兒，身死而殃及祖禰。

translations.literal: Zai flattered Fuguo to advance himself, manipulated timely power to secure his post, public anger was hard to offend yet he long persisted in evil without repenting—his house perished and punishment reached wife and children; his body died and calamity reached grandparents and forebears.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Zai fawned on Li Fuguo to rise, manipulated power to hold his place, and though public wrath mounted he never reformed. His house was destroyed, his wife and children executed, and even his ancestors' graves were violated.

sentences.zh: 縉附會奸邪，以至顛覆。

translations.literal: Jin attached himself to treacherous evil, reaching downfall.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jin attached himself to the wicked and was brought to ruin.

sentences.zh: 炎隳崔祐甫之規，怒段秀實之直，酬恩報怨，以私害公。

translations.literal: Yan destroyed Cui Youfu's regulations, was angry at Duan Xiushi's uprightness, repaid favors and avenged grudges, harming the public with private ends.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yan tore down Cui Youfu's policies, resented Duan Xiushi's integrity, repaid debts and settled scores, and let private interest harm the public good.

sentences.zh: 三子者鹹著文章，殊乖德行。

translations.literal: The three men all distinguished themselves in literary composition, yet were utterly at odds with moral conduct.
translations.idiomatic: All three were accomplished writers, yet their conduct fell far short of their talent.

sentences.zh: 「不常其德，或承之羞」，大《易》之義也。

translations.literal: "If one does not constantly maintain one's virtue, one may inherit disgrace"—this is the meaning of the great Book of Changes.
translations.idiomatic: "If one does not constantly maintain one's virtue, one may inherit disgrace"—so says the Great Book of Changes.

sentences.zh: 富貴不以其道，小人之事哉！

translations.literal: Wealth and honor not by the Way—are these not the affairs of petty men!
translations.idiomatic: Wealth and honor gained without the Way—are these not the ways of petty men!

sentences.zh: 觀庾準之憸，遭王縉之復，徇楊炎之意，曲致劉晏之冤。

translations.literal: Observing Yu Zhun's sycophancy, encountering Wang Jin's restoration, following Yang Yan's intent, he bent matters to bring about Liu Yan's injustice.
translations.idiomatic: Consider Yu Zhun's sycophancy: favored by Wang Jin's return to power, he carried out Yang Yan's will and contrived the wrongful death of Liu Yan.

sentences.zh: 積惡而獲令終者，其在余殃乎！

translations.literal: One who accumulates evil yet obtains a good end—perhaps the remaining calamity lies there!
translations.idiomatic: That one who piled up evil yet died a peaceful death—perhaps his punishment fell on those who came after!

sentences.zh: 贊曰：載、縉、炎、準，交相附會。

translations.literal: The eulogy says: Zai, Jin, Yan, and Zhun attached themselves to one another in mutual collusion.
translations.idiomatic: Eulogy: Yuan Zai, Wang Jin, Yang Yan, and Yu Zhun colluded with one another.

sentences.zh: 《左傳》有言，貪人敗類。

translations.literal: The Zuo Commentary has a saying: the greedy man ruins his kind.
translations.idiomatic: The Zuo Commentary says that the greedy man ruins his kind.
